articles.title: Pacers' Tyrese Haliburton Claps Back at Bucks Fan After Throwing Out 1st Pitch at Cubs Game
articles.summary: Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton took some time to push back against a fan who criticized him for throwing out a first pitch for the Chicago Cubs despite growing up as a Milwaukee Brewers fan.
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton took some time to push back against a fan who criticized him for throwing out a first pitch for the Chicago Cubs despite growing up as a Milwaukee Brewers fan.

Haliburton responded to a post criticizing him of "going out of his way" to root against Milwaukee by screenshotting previous posts from the same user praising his play.

Winners and Losers from Clippers Ruling 📊

The social media spat took place after Haliburton made a Thursday night appearance at Wrigley Field ahead of the Cubs' 2-1 win over the visiting Brewers.

Haliburton said in an April 2025 appearance on the Pat McAfee Show he was no longer a Brewers fan because the club had rescinded an invitation to throw out a ceremonial first pitch in 2024.

At that time, the Pacers had just eliminated the Milwaukee Bucks from a second consecutive first round of the NBA playoffs.

The clubs avoided the same matchup last season by both falling short of the playoffs as Haliburton sat out the campaign with the Achilles injury he suffered during the 2025 NBA Finals.

Haliburton is now preparing to make his comeback after more than a year away when the Pacers open the regular season Oct. 21 at the New Orleans Pelicans.

articles.title: NBA 2K27 predicts the season: LeBron's shocking start with 76ers, a new MVP and an NBA Finals rematch
articles.summary: For the third year in a row, Yahoo Sports is simulating a full NBA season in the latest entry in the NBA 2K franchise — NBA 2K27.
articles.body:
For the third year in a row, Yahoo Sports is simulating a full NBA season in the latest entry in the NBA 2K franchise — NBA 2K27.

Last year's simulation proved to be shockingly accurate. Not only did NBA 2K26 predict the Knicks to win the NBA Finals and Jalen Brunson to be named NBA Finals MVP, it also nailed Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's repeat bid for MVP, Victor Wembanyama's Defensive Player of the Year nod and Cooper Flagg's Rookie of the Year victory. It even had the Wizards as the league's worst team, albeit with half of the wins the real-life version managed to muster.

All things considered, it was safe to say one of the best simulation video game experiences on the market walked the walk.

For those new to this series, here are the rules: We select one team, at random (Miami Heat) and run through a MyEras season with CPU trade offers turned off, with G-League, scouting and rotational decisions set to automatic. The simulation is halted to record the NBA Cup winner, at the end of the regular season and before the NBA Finals.

(Disclaimer: Although the NBA has ruled in the Kawhi Leonard-Clippers investigation, Leonard's trade to the Raptors remains in limbo, so for this simulation he is still a member of the Clippers roster.)

Much like last year, before the simulation fully got underway, we were prompted that LeBron James would be retiring — despite signing a two-year deal with the Sixers — and offered the option to have him do a retirement tour.

Since we'd be simulating everything anyway, we declined.

That housekeeping item aside, there's no way to sugarcoat how James' first — and perhaps only — season with the Sixers went, according to NBA 2K27. In what will wind up being his age-42 season, James played 77 games and finished with career lows in minutes per game (30.5), points (16.9) and assists (4.9). Even his rebounding average (5.6) was the lowest total since his rookie season.

If James' struggles weren't enough of a surprise, the revamped Sixers were the biggest shocker of the entire simulation, and not in a good way. Philadelphia, after adding James and trading for Jaylen Brown, finished 14th in the Eastern Conference with a record of 27-55. Brown's scoring took a major dip, dropping more than seven points per game, and his scoring (21.5) and assist (3.3) averages were the lowest since the 2019-20 season.

Injuries did not play a major role in Philadelphia's nightmare season, as only Tyrese Maxey missed significant time (20 games) of the projected starting lineup of Brown, James, Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and Joel Embiid.

Considering the talent and level of expectations surrounding the 76ers, this was easily the least feasible outcome of anything that happened in the 2K27 simulation.

No, it wasn't the Mavs for a third consecutive year.

This time, the NBA's best record belonged to the Minnesota Timberwolves, who reloaded their roster in an attempt to surround Anthony Edwards with a championship-caliber supporting cast during his prime.

In NBA 2K27, the experiment worked, as Minnesota finished with the best record in the NBA (63-19), with Chris Finch taking home Coach of the Year honors. The Wolves finished as a top-3 team in both offense and defense, and the pairing of Edwards and LaMelo Ball was lethal. Ant-Man finished second in the league in scoring (29 PPG) and Ball was fifth in assists (7.5 APG).

The Bucks were the NBA's worst squad, which shouldn't come as a huge surprise considering the heavy rebuild in the wake of the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade this offseason. Milwaukee finished 24-58 and had a bottom-10 squad on both the offensive and defensive sides of the ball.

GTA VI isn't the only hotly anticipated, Miami-related debut this fall, as Antetokounmpo is set to play for a non-Bucks team for the first time in his career.

Unfortunately for Antetokounmpo and the Heat, things did not start off well. Before the month of November was over, Antetokounmpo (right hand fracture), Tim Hardaway Jr. (broken ankle), and Bam Adebayo (twisted knee) were all shelved for multiple weeks. Bobby Portis would suffer a season-ending knee injury in February.

Despite all of the injuries, Miami did manage to make the playoffs, finishing 38-44, good for the ninth seed in the Eastern Conference, and Antetokounmpo was named the NBA's Clutch Player of the Year, finishing with 21.7 points per game, 11.1 rebounds, 5.6 assists and 2.9 stocks.

Miami was ousted in the first round of the play-in tournament by the Bulls.

The in-season tournament final featured the defending Cup and NBA champion Knicks against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Led by NBA Cup MVP Gilgeous-Alexander, the Thunder took down the Knicks in what would be an ominous sign for New York.

Most Valuable Player — Although Gilgeous-Alexander led the NBA in scoring (31.9 PPG), the Victor Wembanyama Era officially got underway in NBA 2K27. Wembanyama — who won Defensive Player of the Year in the simulation as well — finished the season averaging 25 points per game, 13.1 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 4.9 stocks. While Wembanyama will continue to face stiff competition from both Gilgeous-Alexander and Nikola Jokić in the MVP race, this feels like more of an inevitability for the 22-year-old, assuming he stays healthy.

Rookie of the Year — Memphis' Cameron Boozer edged No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa to become the second consecutive Duke player to win the award. Boozer finished with averages of 13.5 points and 7.7 rebounds for the Grizzlies, while Dybantsa averaged 10.8 and 4.9 in the same categories for the Wizards.

Coach of the Year — Chris Finch, Timberwolves

Defensive Player of the Year — Victor Wembanyama, Spurs

Sixth Man of the Year — Jalen Green, Suns

Most Improved Player — Zaccharie Risacher, Mavericks

Clutch Player of the Year — Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat

The NBA 2K franchise must really love the Knicks, because for the third year in a row, New York is playing for the (simulated) Larry O'Brien trophy. The Knicks finished with the second seed in the Eastern Conference and marched through the bracket, with Jalen Brunson winning East Finals MVP by averaging 31.3 points per game. Waiting for him on the other side was a familiar foe.

San Antonio, led by league MVP Wembanyama, took down the No. 1 seed Timberwolves in the West finals, with Wembanyama adding to his trophy case in the process.

In the rematch of the actual NBA Finals from last year, the script was flipped entirely, with the Spurs sweeping the Knicks in dominant fashion. In Game 2 and Game 4, Wembanyama finished with 20-plus rebounds and had an astonishing eight blocks in the closeout game. Wembanyama finished the series averaging 26.5 points, 18.2 rebounds, 5.3 assists and seven stocks, earning the Bill Russell NBA Finals MVP Award.

If Wembanyama were to win NBA MVP, be named Defensive Player of the Year and capture the NBA Finals MVP Award, he would join Hakeem Olajuwon as the only players in NBA history to do so in the same season.

articles.title: Ben Simmons reportedly agrees to 1-year, $3.5M deal with Kings
articles.summary: The 30-year-old Simmons did not play in the NBA last season.
articles.body:
Ben Simmons is returning to the NBA after reportedly signing a one-year, $3.5 million contract to join the Sacramento Kings, according to ESPN's Marc Spears and Shams Charania .

He is expected to be a backup point guard for rookie Darius Acuff Jr.

The 30-year-old Simmons last played in the NBA during the 2024-25 season with the Los Angeles Clippers. After his contract expired following that season, he did not sign anywhere in free agency and reportedly turned down a one-year minimum contract offer from the New York Knicks.

Simmons had a productive first four NBA seasons with the Philadelphia 76ers, where he won Rookie of the Year and averaged double-digits in points. The 2021-22 season saw him hold out and ask to be traded, which led to a move to the Brooklyn Nets.

Back injuries limited Simmons' time on the court in Brooklyn and he eventually underwent surgery for a herniated disc. He was waived by the Nets in Feb. 2025 and had his contract bought out. Two days later, he signed with the Clippers.

As his NBA future remained in limbo, Simmons was a full participant at a player-led minicamp for the Australian men's basketball team in August with the 2028 Olympics in his sights.

Not long after that camp, Simmons worked out for Kings general manager Scott Perry in Miami and later flew to Sacramento to visit with head coach Doug Christie and his staff.

Simmons kept busy last season, just not focused solely on basketball. He purchased a controlling stake in the South Florida Sails Angling Club , a professional sports fishing team. In May, the team won the 2026 SFC Walker's Cay Open Championship .

The 2016 No. 1 overall pick in the NBA Draft is a three-time All-Star and two-time All-Defensive First Team selection. Over 383 career games, he's averaged 13.1 points, 7.4 rebounds, 7.2 assists, and 1.5 steals per game.

articles.title: El Mundial arranca con récord de un rival de España: 20 triples para Japón con nueve de Hayashi
articles.standfirst: La selección japonesa supera a Mali por 102-97 en el partido inaugural
articles.summary: La selección japonesa supera a Mali por 102-97 en el partido inaugural
articles.body: El Mundial Femenino arrancó con récord en un partido que enfrentó a los dos siguientes rivales de España. En el partido inaugural del torneo, Japón se impuso a Mali por un apretado 102-97. La selección asiática confirmó su fama de equipo tirador y anotó 20 triples, nueve de ellos de Saki Hayashi. Las dos marcas son topes en el campeonato. Japón igualó el mejor registro en la historia del Mundial Femenino. Lo poseía ella misma desde que en 1994 también hiciera 20 triples en un encuentro frente a Kenia. Hayashi, mientras, superó los ocho aciertos en los que estaba el techo en poder de la surcoreana Beon Yeon-Ha (2002) y de la cubana Gricel Herrera Méndez (1998). La escolta nipona, sin embargo, no se mostró del todo satisfecha con su actuación, finalizada con 27 puntos tras hacer 9/15 desde el arco. "Obviamente, estoy contenta, pero mi trabajo es simplemente tirar. En el vestuario se da por hecho que voy a tirar triples. Sin embargo, anoté nueve, pero fallé los dos primeros. Tengo que volver a trabajar", dijo. Su seleccionador Corey Gaines se deshizo en elogios hacia ella: "He entrenado en la WNBA y la NBA, he jugado en la FIBA y la Euroliga y no juzgo a una jugadora hasta que la veo entrenar todos los días. He visto a 'Kiki' durante muchos años y es una de las mejores tiradoras que he visto". Por supuesto, a golpe de triple, Japón acabó con la resistencia de Mali, que será el rival de España en la mañana de este sábado. Las africanas llegaron a tener 10 puntos de renta en el tercer periodo (61-71), gracias al poderío interior de Aminata Sangaré (22 puntos con 9/9 en tiros de dos y ocho rebotes) y Sika Kone (21+11, siete ofensivos). Pero su última ventaja fue a falta de 4:41 para el final (84-85). Ahí el partido se redujo al acierto exterior de las japonesas contra el dominio de Sangaré en la zona. La pívot hizo 10 puntos casi seguidos para mantener las opciones de su equipo, pero un acierto de Maki Takada a falta de 48 segundos fue determinante (101-95). En la última posesión, Mali atrapó cinco rebotes en ataque pero fue incapaz de anotar y apretar aún más el marcador.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown's GoPro Found at Bottom of Ocean by USA Swimmers Patrick Sammon, Michael Andrew
articles.summary: Team USA swimmers Patrick Sammon and Michael Andrew say they didn't recognize Jaylen Brown when reviewing footage of the Philadelphia 76ers star on a GoPro they found on the ocean floor in Hawaii.
articles.body:
Team USA swimmers Patrick Sammon and Michael Andrew say they didn't recognize Jaylen Brown when reviewing footage of the Philadelphia 76ers star on a GoPro they found on the ocean floor in Hawaii.

Sammon launched their search for the lost camera's owner by sharing footage of Brown paddling on a surfboard and asking followers to help identify him.

"As soon as we turned it on, we were like, 'Oh, this guy looks super familiar,'" Sammon said in an interview shared Friday by USA Swimming. "This guy is, like, seven feet tall, and there's a mic boom over his head, so you could see he has a full-on camera crew. And we're like, 'Alright, we've got to figure out who this guy is.'"

The swimmers' discovery quickly went viral after Sammon posted the video of Brown in late August.

"Anyone know who this is? Tag him if you do," Sammon wrote on the video. "Help me find him so I can give him his footage back + a free swim lesson lol."

Sammon said he received responses within the first two minutes of posting asking him if he really didn't know the video featured Brown.

Should Brown take Sammon up on his offer of lessons, it wouldn't be his first time learning from a professional. He said last October he had been recently taught by former U.S. Olympic swimmer and Boston College swim coach Dara Torres.

articles.title: USA vs. China Box Score, Reaction from 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup Group Ahead of KO Bracket
articles.summary: Team USA got its title defense off to an impressive start Friday at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, defeating China 94-61 in its opening game of group play.
articles.body:
Team USA got its title defense off to an impressive start Friday at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, defeating China 94-61 in its opening game of group play.

Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers, Rhyne Howard and Jackie Young all scored in double figures for the Americans in what was a one-sided affair.

Making her FIBA World Cup debut, Clark was the standout for the United States, as the Indiana Fever star was the only American to post a double-double with 14 points and 11 assists.

Clark, who came off the bench, had just five points at halftime, but they were of the impressive variety, as she absorbed contact to make a layup and drilled a long three-pointer:

She truly hit her stride during the second half, helping Team USA balloon its 20-point halftime lead to 33 by the end of the game.

Clark looked the part of the United States' best player on Friday, and she garnered plenty of praise on social media because of it:

As excellent as Clark's performance was, the even more encouraging takeaway from Friday's game for the U.S. may have been its smothering team defense.

The Americans held China to just 32 percent shooting from the field and 26 percent shooting from beyond the arc. Team USA also forced 16 turnovers.

That style of play figures to serve the United States well regardless of who it plays in Berlin, as the Americans look to win their fifth consecutive FIBA Women's World Cup.

They will return to action Sunday for another Group D game against Italy before finishing group play Monday against Czechia.

Assuming Team USA wins Group D as expected, it will begin knockout round action on Thursday.

articles.title: España - Alemania en directo | Mundial de baloncesto femenino 2026 hoy en vivo
articles.summary: 15 asistencias para España por 2 de Alemania en los primeros 20 minutos. Una bestialidad. Se quedó Iyana con un cómodo tiro, pero no pudo anotar. Perf
articles.body:
Última hora del España - Alemania en directo:

¡¡¡Muy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a todos y todas al Mundial Femenino de Baloncesto 2026 de Alemania !!! La selección española realiza su debut en este primer día de torneo ante la anfitriona , con toda la ilusión por conseguir algo grande este verano. Tras perderse la última cita mundialista, España regresa a todo lo grande con un equipo de absoluta garantía y entre las que figuran cinco jugadoras de la WNBA , por primera vez en su historia. María Conde , Raquel Carrera , Awa Fam , Alicia Flórez y Megan Gustafson viajaron desde el otro lado del charco para sumarse al resto de las jugadores que completan la convocatoria: Paula Ginzo , Helena Pueyo , Mariona Ortiz , Alba Torrens , Maite Cazorla , además de Elena Buenavida e Iyana Martín , que se podrían incorporar también en breves a la liga norteamericana.

Las de Miguel Méndez llegan a este Mundial tras un 3-2 en la clasificación, con victorias sobre Puerto Rico , Senegal y Nueva Zelanda , y dos derrotas ante Italia y Estados Unidos, la máxima favorita para levantar su decimosegundo trofeo. Sin embargo, respecto a los partidos previos para preparar este campeonato, España ha hecho un pleno. Cuatro victorias contra, precisamente, Alemania , Nigeria , Bélgica y Mali , quien también queda encuadrada en el grupo A, además de Japón.

Más allá de los Mundiales , España viene recientemente de conseguir dos platas consecutivas en los Eurobasket 23 y 25 después de perder ambas finales ante su verdugo, Bélgica. En los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024 también cayó ante las europeas, en cuartos de final . Y esta rivalidad no entiende de competiciones; en el último Mundial que disputó España , ganó el partido por el tercer y cuarto puesto a las belgas para colgarse el bronce.

La Selección llega a este torneo con todas las expectativas, y sin miedo a nadie, como dejó claró su seleccionador : "La bendita inconsciencia hace que no temamos a nadie" , declaró a MARCA . También Iyana Martín y Awa Fam dijeron en una entrevista a este periódico que este equipo tan joven "se muere por ganar". Por lo pronto, FIBA pronostica al equipo nacional como tercera favorita para levantar la Copa del Mundo , sólo por detrás de Estados Unidos y Francia . Veremos qué nos tiene deparado esta Selección que pocas veces falla a su cita con el metal , en un torneo que apenas dura 10 días , con la final el próximo domingo 13 de septiembre . Aquí viviremos todos los partidos de España , y hoy te acompañamos para vivir el primero de ellos. Desde las 17:45 , contra Alemania y, como siempre, en MARCA .

articles.title: Inside a Louisiana courtroom': SEC-LSU legal circus played out like a John Grisham novel in stunning showdown
articles.summary: Greg Sankey snuck into a Baton Rouge courtroom as the SEC filed a bombshell federal lawsuit against LSU and Lane Kiffin over eligibility rules.
articles.body: BATON ROUGE, La. — SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey covertly arrived at a Louisiana courtroom Thursday morning more than an hour before the circus was scheduled to begin, just two days before LSU was set to welcome Clemson to "Death Valley.," Around the same time Sankey took his seat, Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill stepped out of a government vehicle and made her way inside. Before entering, however, she made her allegiance clear. LSU MIGHT HAVE TO SUE THE SEC IF THIS LEGAL WAR IS EXPEDITED, WHILE DABO SWINNEY IS STAYING IN HIS 'LANE' "Go Tigers," Murrill, wearing a purple outfit, proclaimed before blasting both the NCAA and SEC If you didn’t realize the courthouse was just minutes from LSU’s campus, the purple-and-gold atmosphere inside and outside the building made it clear. SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS Television cameras lined the street as reporters waited for everyone connected to the lawsuit to arrive for the highly anticipated showdown. While nearly everyone involved entered through the front door, Sankey slipped in through a side entrance, avoiding the cameras and reporters hoping to ask him questions. Why? The Baton Rouge Sheriff’s Office later released a statement saying Sankey used the side entrance because of threats made against the commissioner before his arrival. Some people associated with the plaintiffs, however, suggested the SEC leader was simply trying to avoid questions. All of that pregame commotion set the stage for what came next. And to put it mildly, Thursday’s hearing was dramatic. SEC drops a bombshell as Louisiana hearing gets underway The conference knew exactly what it was doing Thursday morning. If you thought Sankey traveled to Baton Rouge empty-handed, you haven’t been following the gamesmanship that unfolded behind the scenes in the days leading up to the hearing. Just minutes after Greg Sankey took a seat inside the witness box, a noticeable wave of emotions moved through the courtroom. It was in the early morning hours of Thursday that the Southeastern Conference had initiated a preemptive strike. The SEC had filed a federal lawsuit in Alabama against LSU, head coach Lane Kiffin and athletic department officials alleging that the school was violating First Amendment rights of the conference just as the hearing in Louisiana was getting underway. NCAA CREATED THIS MESS, NOW LSU SET TO MAKE DAE’QUAN WRIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S FIRST NFL RETURNEE The SEC’s lawsuit alleges that LSU was actively recruiting NFL players to return to college while also preventing the conference from enforcing its rules against professional athletes participating in collegiate sports. Simply put, the SEC is furious that LSU has challenged the conference’s attempts to enforce its eligibility rules for athletes returning from professional sports. NCAA HAS NO PLANS TO SURRENDER, AS ELIGIBILITY LAWSUITS FOR 2022 CLASS TURN INTO AN ALL-OUT LEGAL WAR "Did you authorize the SEC to sue LSU and coach Lane Kiffin?" attorney Tony Clayton asked Sankey. When asked why the conference took that step, Sankey pointed to the authority of the presidents and chancellors he represents. "We established our First Amendment right for freedom of association, so that our conference can make decisions and our members can make decisions about membership," Sankey said. The timing caught the plaintiffs off guard, with attorneys sharing the news amongst them at the table. Clayton asked Sankey three separate times about the conference suing one of its own members before Judge Will Jorden moved the proceedings along. Many expected the hearing to take at least an hour before producing any fireworks. Instead, the SEC’s lawsuit created chaos within minutes of Sankey taking the stand. It was evident that Louisiana court thought timing was too convenient At the core of the lawsuit were athletes such as Dae’Quan Wright, who spent more than 10 hours inside the crowded courtroom, and their argument that they were placed in this position because of the NCAA’s decision not to grandfather the 2022 class into its new eligibility rules. The NCAA recently adopted a five-years-to-play-five-seasons model. However, athletes who would otherwise be eligible under the new guidelines were not included. The dispute has become even more complicated because some members of the 2022 class pursued professional opportunities after exhausting their eligibility under the previous system. One of the central issues discussed Thursday was why the SEC created new guidelines in late August prohibiting athletes who had pursued professional careers from receiving another season of eligibility. The argument against allowing professional athletes to return to college is easy to understand. Most college sports fans would likely agree that a player who has signed with a professional team or participated in a professional training camp should not be allowed to return to the college ranks. However, Clayton used the timing of the SEC’s new guidelines to attack the conference’s position. He questioned whether the rules were created in response to Judge Jorden’s initial temporary restraining order in the case. "That was not re-establishing the rule," Greg Sankey said about the SEC's meeting just over 10 days ago in Brimingham. "The rule was the same rule before and after. The rule was there when I arrived in 2002...What was issued in the memo was consistent with the clarity that was understood by our sixteen universities, and if you have an individual on your roster under that policy, here's the accountability that will be applied." Most people would agree that the SEC’s policy came in response to the series of court orders allowing athletes with professional experience to return to college sports. The Big Ten had already issued similar guidelines before the SEC followed suit. But after listening to Jorden’s arguments before he granted the athletes an injunction, it was clear there was an undercurrent of concern that the conferences had coordinated their actions to undermine his initial ruling. That possibility, however subtle, may have helped drive the legal chaos that unfolded in Baton Rouge just 48 hours before LSU was scheduled to take the field. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Call it Louisiana politics or home-field advantage, but LSU now faces a decision about how to proceed Friday afternoon — a decision that will only heighten the hostile atmosphere around campus throughout the weekend. Now, everyone is waiting to see whether the Tigers will follow through on the chaotic effort to strengthen their roster before the season begins. Or, as we now call it in college athletics, another Friday afternoon courtroom decision.

articles.title: Cathy Engelbert to Retire as WNBA Commissioner at End of 2026
articles.summary: The WNBA announced Friday that commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring from her position at the end of 2026.
articles.body:
The WNBA announced Friday that commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring from her position at the end of 2026.

Engelbert, 61, was named the WNBA's first-ever commissioner in 2019, essentially replacing current NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum, who was the WNBA's interim president from 2018 to 2019.

5 reasons women's FIBA World Cup is must-see TV

In a statement regarding her decision to step away, Engelbert said, "After more than seven years at the WNBA and more than 40 total years in business, I have made the decision to retire as WNBA commissioner. In 2019, I had the privilege of being appointed the league's first commissioner and to lead a league with enormous potential yet untapped awareness and significant undervaluation. Over the years, it has been amazing to watch WNBA players thrive and lead the massive cultural surge around women's sports."

Engelbert has been a polarizing figure during her time as WNBA commissioner, but the growth the league has experienced under her leadership is undeniable.

The WNBA went from a 12-team league when her tenure started to what is soon to be an 18-team league with the additions of expansion teams in Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia from 2028 through 2030.

On top of that, the WNBA currently has $3.1 billion worth of media rights contracts, and the newest collective bargaining agreement, which was ratified in March, resulted in the first $1 million salaries for WNBA players, as well as revenue sharing, per ESPN's Alexa Philippou .

Despite her successes on the business side, Engelbert has been the subject of criticism from WNBA players at times for various reasons, including issues with officiating and poor player salaries and accommodations prior to the current CBA.

Last year, Minnesota Lynx superstar forward and WNBA Players Association vice president Napheesa Collier offered a scathing assessment of Engelbert.

"We have the best players in the world. We have the best fans in the world, but right now we have the worst leadership in the world," Collier said. "If I didn't know exactly what the job entailed, maybe I wouldn't feel this way, but unfortunately for them, I do. We serve a league that has shown they think championship coaches and Hall of Fame players are dispensable and that's fine. It's professional sports, but I will not stand quietly by and allow different standards to be applied at the league level."

It isn't yet known who will succeed Engelbert, but time is running short on her tenure.

Each team has only a handful of regular-season games remaining before the playoffs start this month. The WNBA Finals will then take place next month, signaling the end of the 2026 campaign.

By the time the 2027 WNBA draft is held in April, which is the first major event on the WNBA calendar next year, the league figures to be under new leadership.

articles.title: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert to retire at end of calendar year, ending controversial tenure
articles.summary: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring at the end of the calendar year. Englebert was the first-ever WNBA commissioner in league history, serving in the role for seven years.
articles.body: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring at the end of the calendar year. Engelbert was the first-ever WNBA commissioner in league history, serving in the role for seven years. The news was announced by NBA commissioner Adam Silver. "Cathy has presided over the WNBA through the most significant period of growth in the league’s 30-year history," Silver said in the WNBA’s statement. "We are grateful for Cathy’s leadership and unwavering commitment to the advancement of women’s basketball." Engelbert, 61, has been the commissioner since July 2019. “I retire knowing we have built something bigger, stronger and more enduring than we could have imagined,” she said in a statement. “I am grateful to the WNBA and NBA team owners and staff, players, investors, fans and the powerhouse league office staff, who believed in what this league could become. The league and players didn’t agree to a new collective bargaining agreement until March of this year, and the agreement secured players $1 million salaries for the first time, and also introduced a new revenue-sharing model. Engelbert was named the WNBA’s first commissioner in 2019, as previous leaders of the league held only the title of president. She was challenged soon into her tenure, as the league had to hold its entire 2020 season in a bubble setting in Florida amid the Covid pandemic. articles.summary: La mediática base lidera con 14 puntos y 11 asistencias la paliza de Estados Unidos frente a China
articles.body: Estados Unidos llegó al Mundial Femenino rodeada de ciertas dudas. No por su dominio en los últimos campeonatos planetarios (69-0 desde 2006), sino por las importantes ausencias y el acercamiento de los rivales a su potencial. Pero en el estreno, la gran favorita no dio opción a China en la reedición de la final del último Mundial: 94-61. Buena manera de presentar sus credenciales. También lo hizo Caitlin Clark. La mediática base estadounidense debutó en un gran campeonato siendo la mejor de su selección. Sin llegar a deslumbrar, acabó con 14 puntos (3/7 en triples), 11 asistencias (tope en un estreno mundialista con EEUU) y 22 de valoración en 25 minutos. En el inicio de esta nueva era, otra de las jóvenes llamadas a liderarla, Paige Bueckers, hizo otros 14 puntos y cuatro asistencias después de despertar en la segunda mitad. Estados Unidos marcó territorio desde el inicio. Al final del primer cuarto ya mandaba por 27-14. China apretó en el segundo con un 0-9 para arrancar. La colosal Zhang Ziyu empezaba a imponer sus 2,20 metros, que la convirtieron en la jugadora más alta en la historia del Mundial. Hizo 13 puntos, aunque nueve de ellos llegaron desde el tiro libre. Añadió nueve rebotes. Pero las estadounidenses devolvieron el parcial y las rentas se fueron a los 20 puntos al descanso (49-29). Ya no hubo respuesta de China. Huérfana de su estrella, Li Yueru, que no ha podido estar en el Mundial tras perder el pasaporte, la selección asiática se resignó a la derrota. El doble-doble de Han Xu (11+10) fue muy poco ante el ataque coral de la gran favorita: Rhyne Howard sumó 14 puntos, Jackie Young 12 y la veterana Breanna Stewart añadió 7+7.

articles.title: WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert to retire after 2026 season
articles.summary: Engelbert was named commissioner ahead of the 2019 WNBA season.
articles.body:
WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert will retire at the end of the 2026 season, the league announced on Friday .

"After more than seven years at the WNBA and more than 40 total years in business, I have made the decision to retire as WNBA Commissioner," said Engelbert in a statement. "In 2019, I had the privilege of being appointed the league's first commissioner and to lead a league with enormous potential yet untapped awareness and significant undervaluation. Over the years, it has been amazing to watch WNBA players thrive and lead the massive cultural surge around women's sports."

Engelbert told The Associated Press that she felt the time was right to retire following the "financial transformation journey [the WNBA has] been on." She added that the decision was her own and she did not receive any pressure to step down.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Engelbert was named the league's first-ever commissioner in May 2019 and has overseen two collective bargaining agreement negotiations and helped grow the league via a $3.1 billion media rights deal, as well as the addition of expansion teams. By 2030, the WNBA will have grown from 12 to 18 teams following the additions of franchises in San Francisco, Portland, Toronto, Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia.

Another feather in Engelbert's cap was the COVID-shortened 2020 season played in the "Wubble" at IMG Academy in Florida, avoiding the cancellation of the season amid the pandemic.

"Cathy has presided over the WNBA through the most significant period of growth in the league's 30-year history," said NBA commissioner Adam Silver in a statement. "We are grateful for Cathy's leadership and unwavering commitment to the advancement of women's basketball."

Silver had previously praised Engelbert's work but had been noncommittal about her future, while Engelbert was similarly evasive when asked directly about her plans at July's All-Star Game in Chicago.

Engelbert's tenure has not been without controversy. She was notably criticized over the last year by multiple players calling out her leadership. Napheesa Collier of the Minnesota Lynx said during last year's playoffs that under Engelbert, the league had the "worst leadership in the world." Nneka Ogwumike, head of the WNBA players' union, told ESPN she agreed with Collier's assessment.

While players cooled on their direct criticism of Engelbert after the new CBA was agreed to, the league continues to face challenges as it grows. Among other things, the next commissioner will be faced with addressing the transgender athlete issue that has permeated discussion around the league.

The WNBA has not announced who will succeed the 61-year-old Engelbert as commissioner. She told the AP she has been working on a succession plan for the past year, which will feature internal and external candidates.

"It's a good time to hand it off to the next leader to take the 'W' into a better phase," Engelbert said. "I'm proud of the team we built and everything we accomplished. A leader knows when it's time to drop the mic and move on after building a powerhouse team in the league office."

articles.title: Team USA's kids are all right as youth movement leads dominant effort to open FIBA World Cup
articles.summary: The U.S. women's national basketball team is no stranger to passing the torch at a high rate of success. Though a small sample size, the 2026 World Cup is me...
articles.body:
The U.S. women's national basketball team is no stranger to passing the torch at a high rate of success. Though a small sample size, the 2026 World Cup is merely another example of it working.

Team USA head coach Kara Lawson, making her own national tournament debut, gave the starting nod to the only five returning veterans in the first game of a World Cup that features seven players new to the senior national team. It was the youth core that finished it off, led by an enticing backcourt duo of Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers, who proved again they will be more than worthy carriers of the program's sustained accomplishments.

The U.S. is chasing a fifth consecutive World Cup title while the WNBA rests during an international break for the action. Here's what stood out from a 94-61 win over China , the team's biggest competition in Group D, to open the tournament in Germany on Friday.

Team USA starts veterans in youth-heavy World Cup

Chelsea Gray, Jackie Young, Kahleah Copper, Napheesa Collier and Breanna Stewart, making her USA record-tying fourth World Cup appearance, started the game with a 10-4 lead. At the 6:25 mark, Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston came in for Gray and Collier.

Rhyne Howard was the next in for Copper at 5:16, followed by Paige Bueckers for Young at 4:05. Collier also came back in to keep a veteran on the floor and key Stewart for a breath. Reese made her debut at 1:48 for Boston as the final player into the first quarter, with Team USA holding a 27-12 lead.

The starters returned to the floor together in the third quarter of a 49-29 game. By the 4:42 mark and leading 53-35, Lawson went full youth with Clark, Bueckers, Reese, Howard and Boston on the floor. The veterans didn't touch the floor again.

Young led all veterans with 12 points on 11 attempts. Stewart scored seven on six attempts with seven rebounds.

The Team USA kids are, as always, all right. They outscored China, 41-26, from the 3:53 mark of the third through to the final buzzer. Every player logged at least 11 minutes, and every player scored after late-add Sonia Citron laid in USA's final bucket in the final minute. The reverse layup came off a feed from Clark, who acquired the ball off a Reese block.

Lawson specifically cited a spark from Howard, who led Team USA with 4 3-pointers, when China dropped into a zone in the second half. It was the only extended drought of the game as the U.S. adjusted and China cut it to eight. Howard scored 14, tying a team-high with Clark and Bueckers.

The group games are the best time for Lawson to play with lineups and give the newbies a chance to acclimate. They had about three days in Germany following the final WNBA games on Sunday. The chemistry established by a few of them stateside, namely Fever duo Boston and Clark, helped key some runs.

Team USA is off on Saturday, and will play Italy on Sunday (2:45 p.m. ET) and close out with Czechia on Monday (2:45 p.m. ET). Expect to see deep playing time for the younger players against teams less likely than China to give USA trouble, and potentially even a swap in the starting lineup.

Clark-Bueckers backcourt future is bright

The final quarter showcased the (possibly immediate?) future of Team USA, and there's plenty to be excited about. The ball popped around the floor, led by a dangerous long-term tandem of Clark and Bueckers. The 24-year-olds won golds together at youth national team levels, and will be the backcourt faces of the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. They could also tie Stewart, Sue Bird and Diana Taurasi with four World Cup appearances apiece — they'll be 36 in 2038.

As is required of Team USA players, they're each lighting up in their own specific lane. While both can penetrate the paint and kick out, Clark is taking the role of facilitator as Bueckers eats in the mid-range.

Bueckers shot 5 of 6 from the edge or outside of the paint (she missed one shot inside). She was 6 of 9 overall for 14 points in 20 minutes, adding 4 assists, 2 steals and 2 turnovers.

Clark's historic day answers early questions

Lawson, a hard-nosed defensive coach, is known at Duke to have a short leash for mistakes. There were questions coming in about how patient she might be with Clark's high-risk, high-reward style. But Clark never quite pushed that issue in game 1, and instead earned the distinction of the most assists without a turnover in a World Cup game in Team USA history.

Clark's assists total is the most a Team USA player reached in her debut, cresting Alyssa Thomas' nine in Belgium in 2022. She is one of eight players to have more than 10 assists in a women's World Cup game since the stat was officially recorded in 1994, according to FIBA. And she is the first Team USA player to have at least 10 assists since Dawn Staley had 12 in 1998. That stretch includes World Cups played by Bird and Gray.

Clark opened with four assists in her first four minutes. She hit a trademark deep 3-pointer to open the third quarter as one of her three of the game. The TCL Player of the Game awardee finished with the team's only double-double, scoring 14 (4 of 9) with 11 assists, 3 rebounds and a team-high plus-30.

Clark could easily set the World Cup single-game assists record this year, as well as totals. Julie Allemand of Belgium had 13 in a game in 2018, as did Yuka Harada of Japan in 1994.

The term "cheat code," much like "GOAT," is becoming so overused it's losing meaning. But it is applicable to Chinese 7-foot-3 center Zhang Ziyu.

Zhang holds the ultimate advantage no coach can teach: height. Each time she received the ball in the post, it was akin to a guard mismatched onto a center. Aliyah Boston, at 6-5 the tallest on Team USA, tried her best to contain her, only for Zhang to shoot with ease above her head. The 6-3 Kiki Iriafen might as well have been a GIF of a toddler reaching for a lollipop above an adult's head.

"When she turns and shoots over you, there's nothing you can do," Lawson said in the halftime broadcast interview. "So we'll try and live with those."

Zhang scored 13 points in 18 minutes, tying the team high in points shooting 2 of 4 with two blocks. She was 9 of 10 from the free throw line, double the attempts of any other player in the game. Hinyu Luo had 13 (4 of 10, 3 of 5 from the line), while Han Xu scored 11 on a team-high 14 attempts with 10 rebounds. China missed 6-7 Li Yueru, who was unable to play after her passport was lost in the mail .

What the 19-year-old Zhang lacks is finesse and footwork, skillsets glaring against Team USA's crew but that can be practiced and improved. She is WNBA draft-eligible in the upcoming 2027 draft, and could follow a similar development pattern to national teammate and Liberty center Han (the tallest in the WNBA at 6-11). Zhang currently plays for Hebei Win Power, where she made her professional debut in January.

articles.title: Walter made improper deal with Magic after buying Dodgers: report
articles.summary: Billionaire Mark Walter made an improper deal with business partner Earvin "Magic" Johnson after getting the NBA legend's help in purchasing baseball's Los A...
articles.body:
Billionaire Mark Walter made an improper deal with business partner Earvin "Magic" Johnson after getting the NBA legend's help in purchasing baseball's Los Angeles Dodgers, according to a report on Friday.

In an episode of "Pablo Torre Finds Out", the journalist who last year helped unveil wrongdoing by the NBA's Los Angeles Clippers claimed Walter made hidden arrangements in his $350 million sale of life insurance firm EquiTrust to Johnson, a deal that made Johnson a billionaire.

Sources cited by Torre said the 2015 transaction was repayment by Walter to Johnson for the retired Los Angeles Lakers star using his influence and high profile to help Walter's group win a 2012 bid to buy the Dodgers, who have won the World Series the past two years.

Walter is reportedly the subject of an FBI investigation that some of his firms made unreported affiliated investments, which could put Walter at risk of tax fraud.

Last month, Walter sold the Los Angeles Lakers NBA club for $12.5 billion to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner barely a year after purchasing it from the Buss family for $10 billion.

Walter, through his company TWG Global, said last month that the Dodgers purchase complied with all Major League Baseball rules and regulations and an outside law firm conducted an investigation that found no irregularities in the deal.

Walter's other sports holdings include a share of a holding company that controls English Premier League club Chelsea, France's Strasbourg football team, the Cadillac Formula One team, a professional women's ice hockey league and the Los Angeles Sparks of the Women's NBA.

Torre outlined his report in an appearance on the MSNOW television show "Money Power Politics" on Friday, calling Walter a "one-man stimulus for billionaires owning sports teams" and saying, "Magic Johnson is one of the key figures in this."

"He was sold one of these insurance companies by Mark Walter, his business partner. It made him a billionaire in the process," Torre said.

"They got to together buy and fund the Dodgers using, effectively, law of transitive property via what it means to borrow money, the nest eggs of the parents and grandparents of America who did not realize that this was happening.

"This would be OK if disclosed as a related party transaction... Turns out if America is a land where the rule of law matters, you got to report this. Disclose and tell us the truth because it's not just your money, it turns out he's borrowing against ours."

A year ago, Torre claimed the NBA Clippers and owner Steve Ballmer had improperly avoided league salary cap rules in paying star Kawhi Leonard through business deals with companies that had contracts with the team.

On Wednesday, after an independent investigation and nearly a year after the first report, the NBA pounded the Clippers with some of the harshest punishments in league history, fining the team $30 million and stripping it of five future first-round NBA Draft choices.

The NBA suspended Ballmer from all league and team activities for a year. In a statement, the Clippers vowed to fight the penalties, a challenge that likely means lawsuits against the NBA.

articles.title: Watch Latest LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey Workout in New NBA Offseason Video

The newest Philadelphia 76ers stars continue to put in work alongside Tyrese Maxey.

Trainer Chris Johnson shared a new video on Friday showcasing Maxey, James and Brown running through various actions as they prepare for their first season together in Philadelphia.

James, who signed with the Sixers earlier this offseason to team up with Brown, Maxey and Joel Embiid, has spent time working out with his new teammates several times over the past few weeks.

Brown, who was traded to the Sixers from the Boston Celtics in July, had high praise for his new teammates on a Twitch stream last week.

"Maxey is a dog. LeBron is... you don't even need to say what LeBron is," Brown said. "He looked good, healthy. It's gonna be that. So we working, man. This is one of our first workouts. We worked out a few times. So that's good to just get in the gym with your teammates, get a feel for one another. Feel that the energy level is high, the talent is high. We've just got to come with the right approach. ... LeBron is in his Kobe year, year 24. And we in the birthplace of the Bean. Come on dog, the energy is there."

Philadelphia is an early favorite to take home the 2026-27 title, and for good reason. Even if James is 41 years old and in his 24th season, his late-career skill set should pair nicely alongside the other three stars.

Staying healthy might be the biggest obstacle for the 76ers, but if they can head into the playoffs injury-free, it will be hard for anyone to stop them.

articles.title: España arranca el Mundial con un recital ante el anfitrión
articles.standfirst: La selección de Méndez decide el partido ante Alemania en el descanso (50-24)
articles.summary: La selección de Méndez decide el partido ante Alemania en el descanso (50-24)
articles.body: España no pudo arrancar mejor el Mundial en Berlín. Dio un recital ante Alemania a la que arrasó, 83-53, en un partido para grabar y enseñar en las escuelas. La selección de Miguel Méndez cerró dos cuartos de ensueño tras los que ya tenía el partido casi resuelto (50-24). El baloncesto, a veces, es muy sencillo siempre y cuando se cumplan algunas premisas. Hay que defender, correr, tirar en buenas posiciones tras un buen movimiento de balón y anotar. Todo eso lo hizo España casi a la perfección, sobre todo dos cuartos de ensueño en los que la selección bordó el baloncesto. Si había dudas sobre si la preparación, tan atípica en esta ocasión, podía afectar al juego de España, se despejaron todas en apenas unos minutos. No hubo ni los nervios ni la presión esperada en el estreno, al contrario, la selección jugó con fluidez y mucho acierto muy cerca probablemente de lo que quiere Miguel Méndez a lo largo del campeonato. Bajo la batuta de Iyana Martín, España se marchó muy rápido gracias a su eficacia desde el triple. Alemania, que se sabía inferior en el juego interior, trató de proteger su aro y España reventó la defensa alemana desde el perímetro. Las españolas anotaron sus cinco primeros triples, con María Conde destacando y por eso a 3:48 para el final del primer cuarto ya tenía el choque encarrilado: 24-10 con 6/7 en triples y 8/10 en tiros de campo. España estuvo los 3:48 restantes del acto sin anotar y se fue el minidescanso con 24-13. La defensa española seguía siendo infranqueable para un equipo alemán frustrado. Tardó poco España en anotar cuando nació el segundo cuarto y hacia el ecuador la ventaja ya se acercaba a los 20. El rodillo español seguía engrasado, sobre todo cuando las titulares, Carrera, Conde, Fam, volvieron a pisar la pista. Al descanso, el partido estaba ya roto: 50-24, entre otras cosas por el tiro español, 9/17 en triples, y el alemán 2/15 en tiros de campo en el segundo cuarto, 7/30 (23%) en tiro global y 2/13 en triples. El 15-2 en asistencias era demoledor. España disfrutaba en la pista, no era para menos. Y así siguó en el segundo tiempo donde no hubo más daño porque Alemania intentó tirar de orgullo al inicio del tercer cuarto. Aguantó un poco el vendaval, pero la diferencia entre ambos equipos era abismal. Awa Fam cogió el testigo de los triples de Conde para anotar 3/4 y acabar con 17 puntos, Carrera dominaba los dos aros y firmó el doble-doble (10+10), Conde acabó en 13, e Iyana se fue hasta los 12. Cerca del final, a 5:25, España alcanzó su máxima, 79-47, con la ventaja superando la treintena. Alemania intentaba maquillar lo poco que podía, mientras España sin escatimar esfuerzos seguía ofreciendo minutos muy brillantes a pesar del partido ya ganado. Y Méndez en la banda pidiendo más intensidad, sobre todo defensiva. Esa es la imagen que debe quedar del partido. Además, claro, del juego sobresaliente de un equipo que dejó claro en su estreno que aspira a todo. A TODO.

articles.title: Chris Paul Rips Clippers For Exit in Video, 'One of The Most Disrespectful Things That I've Endured'
articles.summary: Chris Paul is one of the most notable players in Los Angeles Clippers history, but he wasn't exactly treated like a franchise icon during the 2025-26 season.
articles.body:
Chris Paul is one of the most notable players in Los Angeles Clippers history, but he wasn't exactly treated like a franchise icon during the 2025-26 season.

The Clippers sent Paul home in December, ending his time with the team and his NBA career, as he went unsigned for the remainder of the season. Paul called his exit from the team "one of the most disrespectful things that I've endured."

"What's interesting about that whole situation is, it's probably one of the most disrespectful things that I've endured," Paul said. "I've been through a lot of wild stuff in my career, and having older kids and a wife who's very tapped in, and they know the daily goings-on as far as that team and that organization. Obviously I was upset, but my family, my people, everybody... I think just because of the investment we made in the team for as long as we have, and to see the way stuff was handled. What it lets you know is that no matter what you do or what you've done, nobody cares."

Paul returned to the Clippers ahead of the 2025-26 campaign and hoped to get a retirement tour from the franchise where he had his best years, but things quickly went south.

Paul reportedly butted heads with the coaching staff and front office, and it ultimately led to his exit.

The legendary point guard didn't get the send-off he probably deserved, but he'll at least get a warm welcome into the Hall of Fame when the time comes.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Potential Kevin Love, T-Wolves Reunion After Jonathan Kuminga Contract
articles.summary: A potential reunion between Kevin Love and the Minnesota Timberwolves could be in the works.
articles.body:
A potential reunion between Kevin Love and the Minnesota Timberwolves could be in the works.

The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski said this week that both sides have some level of interest in working out a deal before the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

"From what I understand, Kevin Love is open to coming back to Minnesota. I do think the Wolves have some interest in bringing him back as well," Krawczynski said on his podcast (h/t HoopsHype ). "It would just be a phenomenal story if the Wolves did decide to fill that spot, and they did it with Kevin Love."

Love, 37, started his career with the Timberwolves in 2008 and had some of his best seasons in Minnesota. He was traded to the Cleveland Cavaliers ahead of the 2015 campaign, and he'd go on to win a title alongside LeBron James and Kyrie Irving.

Love has since bounced around, spending a few years with the Miami Heat before playing for the Utah Jazz last season. Now, he's a free agent and has the chance to decide where he'll spend what could be his last season.

While Love is far from his prime, he could still be a solid option off the bench for Minnesota. More importantly, he could be a veteran voice on a team full of young talent.

articles.summary: María Conde muestra su malestar por haber acabado el primer partido a las 19.26 y tener que arrancar el segundo a las 11.30
articles.body: La selección española terminaba su sensacional debut en el Mundial Femenino ante Alemania este viernes a las 19.26. Este sábado, a las 11.30, volverá a jugar. Entre el final de un partido y el inicio del otro sólo habrán pasado 16 horas. En una tesitura pocas veces vista en un torneo internacional, afrontará con un mínimo descanso la segunda cita. Será frente a Mali. Esta ajustada agenda supondrá un riesgo para la salud de las jugadoras y obligará a cambiar horarios y rutinas. Después del primer partido, atención a medios, ruedas de prensa, traslado al hotel, cena nada más llegar, tratamientos con los fisioterapeutas y a dormir cuanto antes, que toca madrugar. Este sábado, se adelantará el toque de diana. El desayuno será de 7.30 a 8.30, media hora después habrá sesión de vídeo y a las 9.30 saldrán para el Max Schmeling Hall, donde se disputará el encuentro. Por supuesto, no se podrá realizar la sesión de tiro, como suele hacerse en la mañana antes de los encuentros. En la expedición española hay una entendible molestia por los horarios. “Hay que darle una vuelta al calendario. FIBA tendrá que repensarlo porque se habla de darle prioridad a los deportistas, pero no está pasando y no vamos a tener ni 12 horas para descansar”, lamentaba María Conde. Ante la falta de tiempo, el cuerpo técnico ha preparado los dos primeros partidos del Mundial al mismo tiempo. “Es lo que hemos tenido que hacer en cuanto a estudio de los rivales. Hemos venido con dos planes de partido diferentes”, explica el seleccionador Miguel Méndez. Para prepararse ante esta situación, la FEB ya programó dos partidos en días consecutivos en el triangular que se celebró en Zaragoza, aunque no con tan poco tiempo de descanso. Ahí, la selección se midió primero a Mali, precisamente, y al día siguiente a China en el último amistoso antes de viajar a Berlín. Aquel encuentro frente al conjunto africano, aún sin las jugadores provenientes de la WNBA, fue poco más que un entrenamiento con público: 97-58. Mali, número 18 en el ránking FIBA, es un combinado que destaca especialmente por su músculo. “Será un partido muy exigente en lo físico, pero también en cuanto a baloncesto porque tienen jugadoras que son estrellas en la Liga Femenina Endesa y están muy acostumbradas a jugar en Europa”, analiza Méndez. Aminata Sangaré, ala-pívot del Leganés de 1,85 metros, y Sika Kone, pívot de 1,90 del CAB Estepona, son dos de sus referentes.

articles.title: La comisionada de la WNBA se jubilará en pleno debate sobre las atletas transgénero
articles.standfirst: Cathy Engelbert dejará su cargo tras un agitado mandato de siete años y medio
articles.summary: Cathy Engelbert dejará su cargo tras un agitado mandato de siete años y medio
articles.body: La comisionada de la WNBA, Cathy Engelbert, se retirará al final del año, lo que pondrá fin a sus más de siete años al frente de la liga y a una gestión que ha sido transformadora y, por momentos, tumultuosa. Engelbert es la segunda presidenta o comisionada de la WNBA con más tiempo en el cargo, y ayudó a negociar un lucrativo convenio colectivo esta pasada primavera que dio como resultado el primer conjunto de salarios de un millón de dólares para jugadoras en la liga. "Cathy ha presidido la WNBA durante el periodo de crecimiento más significativo en los 30 años de historia de la liga", comentó el viernes Adam Silver, comisionado de la NBA, al anunciar la decisión de Engelbert. "Estamos agradecidos por el liderazgo de Cathy y su compromiso inquebrantable con el avance del baloncesto femenino". Engelbert, que cumplirá 62 años en noviembre, le dijo a The Associated Press que lleva meses pensando en retirarse. "Cuando llegué por primera vez a la liga, mi intención era hacer esto durante 3 años y medio. Los 7 años y medio superaron ese tiempo", explicó en entrevista telefónica. "Este es un momento realmente bueno, dado el recorrido de transformación financiera en el que hemos estado. Lograr el convenio colectivo, cerrar un acuerdo de derechos de medios a largo plazo, concretar la expansión". Engelbert insiste en que la decisión de irse fue únicamente suya y que no sintió presión alguna para dejar el cargo por parte de actores de la NBA o de la WNBA. La comisionada señaló que ha estado trabajando en un plan de sucesión durante los últimos años. Aunque no dio detalles sobre quién podría ser considerado para el puesto, Engelbert sí indicó que hay posibles candidatos, tanto internos como externos, en el radar de la liga. "Es un buen momento para entregárselo al próximo líder, para llevar la 'W' a una mejor etapa", indicó. "Estoy orgullosa del equipo que construimos y de todo lo que logramos. Un líder sabe cuándo es momento de soltar el micrófono y seguir adelante después de construir un equipo potente en la oficina de la liga". Engelbert comentó que tiene sentimientos encontrados sobre su salida. "Me encanta el baloncesto femenino y todavía no me voy a ninguna parte. Llevaremos a cabo un verdadero proceso de sucesión en los cuatro meses que quedan. Si no encontramos a alguien, me quedaré. Yo no tuve transición. Entré por la puerta y estaba sola, porque nadie me hizo una transición hacia este rol". "Ojalá pueda ayudar a que este próximo líder tenga una transición, especialmente considerando el ascenso de esta liga". La WNBA ha crecido a un ritmo exponencial durante el mandato de Engelbert como comisionada, con récords de audiencia televisiva, una asistencia sólida, un nuevo acuerdo de derechos de medios a largo plazo y una expansión a 18 equipos para finales de la década. "Me trajeron como líder empresarial para transformar el negocio. Yo miro los ingresos y la mercancía, la audiencia y la asistencia", expresó Engelbert y señaló cómo todos han mejorado. "Un gran líder percibe cuándo es momento de que alguien más llegue. Cuando yo llegué, esta liga enfrentaba preguntas sobre nuestra viabilidad y sostenibilidad a largo plazo". Engelbert afirmó que el crecimiento de la liga ha "superado con creces sus expectativas" desde que asumió el cargo tras dejar su puesto anterior como presidenta de Deloitte en 2019. Además del nuevo convenio colectivo, la lista de cosas de las que se siente más orgullosa incluye haber conseguido viajes chárter para las jugadoras, mantener la liga en marcha durante la pandemia de coronavirus, el histórico acuerdo de derechos de medios y el aumento exponencial del valor de las franquicias de la WNBA. En 2019, el valor promedio de una franquicia de la WNBA era de 10 millones de dólares; en 2026, es de aproximadamente 460 millones de dólares. Sin embargo, junto con las ganancias financieras, la agitación y la tensión han acompañado el crecimiento de la WNBA. Las jugadoras dicen que han visto más comentarios negativos en redes sociales dirigido hacia ellas en los últimos años y algunas no sienten que la liga haya hecho lo suficiente para garantizar su seguridad. La liga también ha estado en el centro de debates sobre atletas transgénero que juegan en la liga. Engelbert ha dicho repetidamente que los ataques en línea contra las jugadoras son inaceptables y respalda iniciativas de la liga para protegerlas. También sostuvo que no debería haber confusión sobre la cuestión transgénero. "No tenemos problemas actuales de elegibilidad en la WNBA", afirmó y añadió que "si los tuviéramos, tendríamos una discusión reflexiva sobre políticas con el (sindicato de jugadoras) y las jugadoras". Aunque durante las recientes negociaciones del convenio colectivo hubo una relación tensa entre la comisionada y las jugadoras, Engelbert insiste en que mantiene una buena relación con ellas. Las conversaciones entre la comisionada y las jugadoras han sido complicadas. Breanna Stewart, alera del New York Liberty y vicepresidenta del comité ejecutivo del sindicato de jugadoras de la WNBA, dijo antes del Juego de Estrellas que entre las jugadoras hay respeto por Engelbert, pero no mucha relación.

articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com. I know all eyes are on the Commonwealth today (sickening, by the way), but let's all just take a step back for a second and enjoy the simpler things in life. We're here. An actual college football Friday. Labor Day weekend. One of the most underrated weekends of the entire calendar year. WEEK ONE UPSET SPECIAL: THESE THREE COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS SHOULD BE ON UPSET ALERT THIS WEEKEND Football last night. Football tonight. And tomorrow. And the next day. And the day AFTER that! But wait, there's more! After Monday, we take a full 48 hours off before the NFL season kicks off on Wednesday. Lordy. She's here, and she's just as beautiful as I imagined. How lucky are we? What a blessing. Let's roll. Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham supports the vets like a patriot, and then gets us fired up for football season ... again, like a patriot. What else? I've got a poor woman getting trucked on the sidelines in Piscataway last night, an absolute UNIT in the high school football ranks, and the Buffaloes were FEELING it after upsetting Georgia Tech. What a scene! OK, grab you whatever you'd like on this first Friday of September — dealer's choice today! — and settle in for a Friday 'Cap! Sophie Cunningham is ready for some college football There she is — your Week 1 viewing schedule. It's perfect. Honestly, though? Not the greatest Week 1 the sport has given us. LSU-Clemson is obviously the headliner tomorrow, but there's not a ton of great games before it. The early games are a slog (except for North Texas-Indiana on FOX, of course!). The 3:30 hour gives us Baylor-Auburn and Boise State-Oregon, for those pining for the old SEC on CBS theme song. CLEMSON'S DABO SWINNEY THROWS SHADE AT LANE KIFFIN, LSU OVER BRINGING IN NFL PLAYERS: 'IT'S EMBARRASSING' Not a ton of competition for LSU-Clemson in the late hour. I don't care, though. It's back. We're back. Thank God. No more WNBA talk ... ... Unless, of course, it involves Sophie Cunningham! She leads us off today. "Spicy Sophie tapping in." Colorado was FEELING it last night She just refuses to miss. Let's put Sophie in the juror pool up in the Commonwealth and see how things play out! "It's the start of a new football season. We are hyped. We're excited. We're about to kick some butt this year. Come out, be loud, and show your Mizzou pride." Sophie gets it. She's just as tired as we are from all the WNBA nonsense. She's ready to get this season started. PS: Sophie welcomed veterans to Gainbridge Fieldhouse all season? Lordy. Absolute patriot. Between that and the return of college football, the left is in shambles today. OK, let's keep this class moving right along. It's a Football Friday, after all. Anyone catch the end of the Colorado-Ga. Tech game last night? I'm not talking about the blocked field goal. I'm talking about what happened after the blocked field goal: Opening night chaos, a high school specimen & '80s mail Look at those maniacs! Big win, and they let the Georgia Tech student section HAVE it. Look at the one player who actually attempts to jump into the stands. Risky little move. He got swatted away like a bug. Probably for the best. I've seen that movie end poorly far too many times. Speaking of last night's appetizer, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into our first BIG weekend of the year. First up? Let's go ahead and check in with the fans up in New Jersey! Incredible. What a game for the UMass Minutemen! First win over an FBS team since 2023! Do you know how much Rutgers paid for that shellacking? $1.5 million. It was the second largest paycheck for a LOSS in college football history: Goodness gracious. The accounts in Piscataway are pulling their hair out today. Just a stunning upset. That wasn't even my favorite part of the game. Anyone here stick around for the postgame fireworks?! Amazing. The obvious question is, why not just cancel the show? I don't know. Can you do that? Can you just cancel a fireworks show because the home team lost? I assume you can just roll them over to the next home game, right? Yikes. Never mind. USC comes to town next. I don't see that first home 'dub coming until Howard the following week. Put those fireworks on ice, fellas! Next? Let's get to some reader mail on the way out. I have a loaded mailbox and it needs a good Labor Day cleaning before we start the fall season. Yesterday, we all mocked Ryan Reynolds for his absolutely baffling comments on how tough the 1980s were to live through ... because of the Cuban Missile Crisis (which ended in the '60s). I asked y'all if there was any truth to it. From Jeff D: As a kid in the 80s , I can’t say that the Cuban Missile Crisis was anywhere at the top of our minds. I do remember a couple of events that were at the top of our minds — the Challenger explosion and baby Jessica being rescued from a well. Baby Jessica was a crazy story of a little girl falling down a well and eventually being rescued, the event really brought the country together and her rescue was a joyous moment for the country. All in all, most memories from that period were positive and I’m pretty sure the Cuban Missile Crisis never crossed our minds. Thanks, Jeff! Would you look at that? A child was in peril in the 1980s and the entire country rallied around her. Weird. Surely that would happen in today's world, right? ... Right? Next? From Brian S: Ryan Reynolds went a bit overboard with the hyperbole, but it wasn’t all fun and games in the 80’s. We 80’s kids lived under the cloud of potential nuclear war for much of the decade. There was a TV movie in 1983 called "The Day After" that terrified the nation. Truly. I think that nuclear war "threat" fed into our, "F–k it, let’s just enjoy ourselves and have a great time" attitude. There was no Cuban Missile Crisis hangover. Vietnam though? Hell yes. Just look at all the movies about that war released during the 80’s. Now, having said all that, I’d give anything to go back there. You often write, "What a time to be alive." Well the 80’s truly embodied that. Thanks, Brian! I may have to look up "The Day After" this weekend. Those things always fascinate me. Finally ... From Eric P: The 80’s was one of the best decades in history. The best music; Cars still had a little style and nothing woke about sports. Oh, and I managed to hit a 3-pointer to win a game at the buzzer over Mark Langston in an alumni game at my college against a team of Mariners. This Reynolds idiot was 8-9 years old and there was no strife. Won’t watch his piece of s–t movie on general principles. Thanks, Eric! I do love the cars from the '80s. One of these day, I want an old 1980s pickup truck. It's a weird dream of mine. Just to drive around town. One of these days. STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW! OK, that's it for today — and this week! It's a High School Football Friday, so let's end class with an absolute UNIT out of Alabama. See y'all Monday. articles.title: Charles Barkley Says He’s Retiring Alongside Ernie Johnson After Next NBA Season
articles.summary: The pair have been on a legendary run on 'Inside the NBA' since 2000, when Barkley joined the show a decade into Johnson hosting.
articles.body:
Charles Barkley has said he's retiring from Inside the NBA alongside host Ernie Johnson after the next NBA season, and this time, it looks like he means it.

"Right now, unless Ernie changes his mind, next year is my last year for 100%," Barkley said on a Thursday episode of The Bill Simmons Podcast .

Johnson has hosted Inside the NBA since 1990 when TNT acquired broadcasting rights, with Barkley joining a decade later after the hall-of-famer retired from the league. Since then, the program has cemented itself as one of the best studio shows on cable despite mostly sidestepping game analysis in favor of alchemized banter. It's a major post-game retention vehicle: In 2025, Inside the NBA averaged 3.5 million viewers following game six of the Pacers-Knicks Eastern Conference Finals versus 8.1 million for the game itself.

This isn't the first time Barkley announced his retirement. He said he'd exit the show amid uncertainty around whether Warner Bros. Discovery would retain NBA broadcasting rights, though he ultimately said he'd stay on shortly before it was announced that the show would be licensed to ESPN as part of Warners' settlement with the NBA.

On the podcast, Barkley said he was ready to retire until Johnson persuaded him to do another season after the show moved under the Disney umbrella.

The only reason I stayed is so that everybody could keep their jobs behind the scenes," he said. "I'm hoping the show keeps going on ESPN, but if Ernie retires after next season, I'm done. I have so much love and respect for that guy. If he says [he's] done, I'm done."

Replacing Johnson will be a tall task. Whoever takes his seat will have to steer a chaotic ship, at times taken over by analysts Shaquille O'Neal and Kenny Smith, both of whom haven't given any indication of retiring. Barkley's seat will be tough to fill as well, though ex-NBA players who've seen their stars rise in the broadcasting and podcasting worlds could be contenders, including Jeff Teague, Kevin Garnett and Richard Jefferson.

articles.summary: In June, Florida football announced a massive renovation project at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. It shouldn't impact home games in 2026, but there's plenty you...
articles.body:
Florida football will be back in the Swamp.

The Gators play their first game under new coach Jon Sumrall on Saturday, Sept. 5, and their first home game since the win over rival Florida State on Nov. 29.

This past offseason, the University Athletic Association announced a $1.45 billion renovation to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium – the most expensive stadium renovation project in college sports history – that will completely transform the facility.

Will those renovations affect the gameday experience for those venturing into the Swamp for the 2026 season?

The short answer? No. Renovations don't begin until after the 2026 season.

In fact, gameday protocols are quite similar to years past in terms of gate opening, parking and road closures.

But for those who have yet to attend a Gator home game, or those who just need a reminder on what to expect, here's what to know before 7:45 p.m. Saturday night vs. FAU.

Florida football offers final preseason glimpse before Sept. 5 opener

What Gainesville roads will be closed for Florida football home games?

Starting five hours before kickoff, Gale Lemerand Drive will be limited to ticket holders only. Three hours before kick, the road completely closes from Stadium Road to University Avenue.

University closes to vehicles starting three hours before kick as well between Gale Lemerand and NW 17th Street, as does Stadium Road from Gale Lemerand to Fletcher Drive. Fletcher is a one-way road this year. Turning south from University Ave is not permitted.

Where to park on UF campus for Florida football home games

Many of the lots closer to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium are reserved. The closest general parking lots are on Fraternity Drive and Woodlawn Drive near Flavet Field.

UF recommends arriving early for general parking lots. Parking on sidewalks is prohibited.

It also recommends parking at either Celebration Pointe, Park and Ride lot #2 at 3497 Hull Road or Garage 109 south of Archer Road on Gale Lemerand Drive and taking a shuttle to the stadium.

When do gates open for Gators games at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium?

Gates open an hour and a half before kickoff and two hours before in premium areas. For the Florida Atlantic game, that is 6:15 p.m. for general and 5:45 p.m. in premium areas.

Once again, tickets are digital. UF recommends adding them to your digital wallet to avoid delays at the stadium. You can also register for express entry, which uses your face instead of showing your ticket.

Tickets are sold out for FAU – the Gators' 19th straight sellout – but tickets are still available on the secondary market .

Where are Florida football cooling stations and restrooms?

Florida football helps fans beat the heat with misting stations throughout Ben Hill Griffin Stadium and free sunscreen at Guest Services Kiosks, located at Gates 1, 7 and 16. Cooling buses are located outside Gates 2 and 13.

Restrooms are available throughout campus. A full list is available here .

What is unique for Florida football vs Florida Atlantic?

The game is designated as 352 Community Day. A portion of every ticket sold will be donated to an Alachua County charity organization. The full list of organizations can be found here. Saturday's battle is also designated as the 2026 Stars of Honor game. It's "a community initiative that rewards local K-12 students with complimentary tickets to a game for academic achievement, character and fitness."

Starting at 4 p.m., fans can watch Florida basketball's open practice inside the O'Connell Center, across the street from the Swamp.

Every fan in attendance will also receive a PixMob LED wristband upon entry that will light up in unison as part of a halftime drone show following the band's performance.

Noah Ram covers Florida Gators athletics and Gainesville-area high school sports for The Gainesville Sun, GatorSports.com and the USA TODAY Network. Contact him at nram@usatodayco.com . Follow him on X @Noah_ram1 , Instagram @Ramreporter and Facebook Noah Ram - Reporter .

articles.title: Caitlin Clark needed one game to break a 28-year-old FIBA World Cup mark
articles.summary: She's the first to do this in seven World Cups.
articles.body:
It took Caitlin Clark all of 25 minutes to end a USA Basketball drought that stretched back to 1998.

Before Clark handed out 11 assists in Team USA's win over China on Friday, no American player had registered double-digit assists in a FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup game since Dawn Staley in 1998.

Staley is now the head coach at South Carolina. Clark is in the third year of her own WNBA career -- and just starting her first competitive tournament with the United States' senior national team.

Clark registered a 14-point, 11-assist double-double against China as the United States rolled to a 94-61 win in Berlin, Germany. More impressively, the Indiana Fever star committed no turnovers, and the US was a plus-30 in her 25 minutes.

It's no surprise Clark touched down in Germany and immediately began slinging passes every which way.

Only Alyssa Thomas has more assists in 2026 than Clark, who is tied with the Phoenix Mercury forward for the league lead with 8.4 assists per game.

"Anybody I pass the ball to, it feels like they're never gonna miss a shot," Clark said after her first World Cup game.

It's easy to feel that way in a star-studded US team, which has taken its first step toward a record-extending 12th World Cup title.
