articles.title: Charles Barkley says he and Ernie Johnson plan to retire from 'Inside the NBA' after this season
articles.summary: 'Unless Ernie changes his mind, next year is my last year.'
articles.body:
Charles Barkley's time with "Inside the NBA" might be coming to a close — though that'll depend on what program host Ernie Johnson decides to do.

On an episode of " The Bill Simmons Podcast " on Friday, Barkley revealed that he and Johnson had agreed to stay on the program for two more years after it moved from TNT to ESPN last season. That means that this coming season will be the last for the duo, unless things change.

The revelation began after Simmons joked that Barkley had "retired" several times but it had never gone through. Barkley, 63, said that he had originally planned to retire from "Inside the NBA" when he turned 60, but they had asked him to stay two more years.

At the point that he was planning to retire, though, TNT lost the media rights to the NBA , leaving the fate of "Inside the NBA" in the balance — something that Barkley was vocally unhappy about at the time. Barkley said he was already retired when Johnson approached him and said that they had struck a deal to bring "Inside the NBA" to ESPN starting in the 2026-27 season.

"Me and Ernie are a package deal," Barkley said. "Ernie said to me, 'Chuck, would you please stay for two more years?' I said, 'I love you, man. You're the best. I'll stay for two more years.' So right now, unless Ernie changes his mind, next year is my last year, 100 percent. … If he says he's done, I'm gone."

Per Barkley, Johnson had pointed out that if they both stayed, the crew members on "Inside the NBA" would get to keep their jobs, which became a motivating factor for them sticking around.

Now, though, this retirement plan would give Johnson, Barkley and co-analysts Shaquille O'Neal and Kenny Smith a chance to stick together for one more year, with the 2026-27 season. Barkley mentioned that his succession plan when he was 60 was for Jamal Crawford and Jalen Rose — both former NBA players with a history with the show — to take over.

Earlier in the conversation with Simmons, Barkley mentioned that he wanted to cut down the amount of time he was on TV, noting that he hadn't been on any ESPN programs since the end of the NBA season.

"The last thing you wanna be is on every show. I don't want people to start getting sick of my face. I'm very strategic," Barkley said.

In addition to revealing his retirement plans, Barkley also dropped that he met with both NBC and Amazon after TNT lost the NBA rights. Per Barkley, NBC offered him a deal, but he declined it.

Barkley joined "Inside the NBA" in 2000, with his brash commentary and dynamic with his fellow hosts helping drive the program's popularity. The last TNT show for "Inside the NBA" happened in May 2025. It debuted on ESPN the following October , with Barkley calling the ability to join the network "an honor and a privilege."

articles.title: Sky Owner Michael Alter Calls Enes Kanter Freedom Lawsuit 'Meritless and Frivolous'
articles.summary: CHICAGO (AP) — Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter says a lawsuit filed by former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom is "meritless and frivolous."
articles.body:
CHICAGO (AP) — Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter says a lawsuit filed by former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom is "meritless and frivolous."

Freedom is alleging that his First Amendment rights were violated when he was ejected from the Sky's WNBA game against the Indiana Fever on Aug. 23. He is seeking damages and the removal of his ban when it comes to attending games at Wintrust Arena.

The lawsuit, filed Thursday in U.S. District Court in Illinois, names Chicago Women's Basketball Operations, LLC, which runs the Sky, the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, the corporation that owns the arena, and the city of Chicago as defendants.

5 reasons women's FIBA World Cup is must-see TV

"Freedom was removed for his conduct, not his speech," Alter said Friday in a statement released by the Sky. "We look forward to the truth prevailing in court."

The 6-foot-10, 250-pound Freedom was removed from the game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter.

Freedom was sitting along the baseline wearing a black shirt that read "WOMAN noun. adult human female."

The Fever called for a timeout after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the period. Cloud then did a chest bump with teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning around and walking in Freedom's direction.

Cloud, 34, started yelling and pointing at Freedom, 34, as she approached him. A standing Freedom held his arms out and stepped onto the court as security and a handful of Sky players moved in between the two.

Freedom stopped near the basket to plead his case to security as he was escorted from the court area. He spun around while holding his shirt out and encouraged the crowd to respond as he walked toward the front lobby.

He had a conversation with a group of police officers before departing the arena.

"The Defendants combined and conspired, and acted jointly to execute their conspiracy, to discriminate against Plaintiff based on Plaintiff's verbal and demonstrable expression of viewpoint and gender identity when they wrongfully ejected Plaintiff from a recent WNBA game," Freedom's lawsuit reads. "Defendants compounded and exacerbated Plaintiff's injuries when they subsequently banned Plaintiff indefinitely from attendance."

Alter announced on Aug. 25 that Freedom was banned from Sky games at Wintrust Arena until he is "able to prove to us to our satisfaction that he is able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat."

In Friday's statement, Alter said Freedom's assertion that he was removed because of his speech was false.

"As his own complaint acknowledges, he wore the shirt in question for multiple hours without any contact with security," Alter said. "Security removed Freedom only after he violated fan code of conduct by rising from his seat, gesturing at a player, and stepping toward the court."

The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women — people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity — should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA.

Although the league's collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. But a person familiar with the decision told the AP that they are not eligible . The person spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitive nature of the situation.

"You don't have to agree with my speech but you don't get to silence me for it," Freedom posted on social media on Thursday. "I will not be intimidated. I will not be silenced. I will continue to stand for women and defend free speech."

articles.title: Cathy Engelbert will be remembered as the commissioner who made the WNBA deeply political and divisive
articles.summary: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced her retirement after 2026, but her seven-year tenure was defined by player clashes and political controversy.
articles.body: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced Friday that she would retire following the 2026 season after seven years in the role. Engelbert took over in 2019 as the WNBA’s first commissioner, and there is no question the league is substantially bigger, more visible and more valuable than when she arrived. The league expanded, secured major media-rights agreements, introduced charter travel and negotiated significant increases in player compensation through a new collective bargaining agreement signed before the 2026 season. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver has called Engelbert’s tenure the most significant period of growth in WNBA history. But does she deserve credit for these successes? I believe the answer is clear. Being commissioner isn’t simply about revenue, television ratings or franchise valuations. A commissioner must also maintain relationships with the players, and those relationships have been objectively tumultuous throughout Engelbert’s tenure. She must protect the league’s reputation and its stars, an area in which she has also fallen short. She must manage controversies, something she has repeatedly failed to do. Finally, she must ensure the on-court product is entertaining and credible, which is arguably the strongest case in her favor. It goes without saying that Engelbert’s tenure has become increasingly contentious, helping lead to her decision to retire. SUE BIRD CLAIMS WNBA PLAYERS WANTED TO 'SHUT UP AND DRIBBLE' DESPITE LEADING 2020 POLITICAL PUSH 1. The 'Wubble' and the league's political transformation Engelbert’s first major test came almost immediately. The COVID-19 pandemic threatened the 2020 season, but the WNBA successfully created the "Wubble" — a play on words combining WNBA and bubble — in Florida and completed the season. While it was a success that the season was able to be played, the league also embraced an increasingly prominent social-justice role. I truly believe this is where the WNBA became the most politically divisive league in America. Players wore social-justice messages, including support for criminal Jacob Blake and Black Lives Matter, which was led by self-described Marxists, and the league partnered with players on racial-justice initiatives. Engelbert allowed all of this to happen and disenfranchised fans who didn’t care for the overt political messaging when they turned to sports as an escape. Engelbert also allowed herself and the league to be bullied by radical left-wing activist players who ousted Atlanta Dream owner and Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler while publicly supporting Raphael Warnock through "Vote Warnock" T-shirts on the court because Loeffler publicly opposed the league’s Black Lives Matter messaging. When the league could have focused on basketball, Engelbert helped the WNBA become completely intertwined with left-wing politics. 2. The Dearica Hamby pregnancy controversy One of the most serious controversies of Engelbert's tenure involved former Las Vegas Aces star Dearica Hamby. Hamby alleged that she experienced bullying and mistreatment after revealing that she was pregnant. The WNBA investigated the situation and determined that the Aces had violated league rules concerning impermissible benefits during contract negotiations involving Hamby. The league punished Las Vegas by taking away a first-round draft pick and suspending coach Becky Hammon for two games. The controversy raised a larger question about how seriously professional sports organizations protect pregnant athletes. It also placed Engelbert in the uncomfortable position of having to demonstrate that the league's commitment to women's sports extended to protecting players who become mothers. 3. The charter-flight controversy For years, WNBA teams primarily traveled commercially because charter flights were considered financially impractical under league economics. That became increasingly controversial as players complained about exhausting travel schedules and safety concerns. The issue became particularly embarrassing for the league because teams had previously been punished for using unauthorized charter flights. Then, in 2024, with the influx of attention, security concerns, and money due to Caitlin Clark, Engelbert announced that the WNBA would introduce a league-wide charter program. Engelbert was right that charter flights didn’t make financial sense before Clark arrived, so I can give her some credit. Ultimately, however, Clark deserves the credit for this, not Engelbert. CAITLIN CLARK CALLS FOR FULL-TIME WNBA REFEREES AS OFFICIATING FAILURES MOUNT IN 2026 4. The Caitlin Clark treatment and officiating controversy The explosion of Clark's popularity also exposed another problem: the WNBA's handling of physical play and officiating. Clark was repeatedly involved in controversial physical incidents, and fans increasingly questioned whether the league was protecting its biggest star. The answer? No. Engelbert was given a gift and she did little to nothing to protect her golden goose. Players and coaches complained about inconsistent officiating, physicality and a lack of accountability. Engelbert eventually announced a committee focused on the "state of the game" and officiating after concerns escalated. The level of incompetence from the top down was damning. Without Clark, the WNBA wouldn't reach new heights and new fans. They needed her for the future of the league and Engelbert was afraid to put her foot down in the wake of immense jealousy, hatred and pettiness from her peers. 5. The "Pay Us What You Owe Us" movement While the WNBA was drawing record attention, another controversy was brewing: money. The league had never made a profit. It always operated on a deficit, but players argued that their compensation wasn't keeping pace with the league's rapidly increasing popularity and revenue. At the 2025 All-Star Game, players wore shirts reading: "Pay Us What You Owe Us." The message was impossible to miss. The dispute centered on the league's revenue-sharing structure and the players' belief that they deserved a significantly larger percentage of the money they were helping generate. The timing was particularly significant. The WNBA was negotiating a new collective bargaining agreement while simultaneously celebrating record ratings, attendance, sponsorships and media-rights revenue. Ultimately, the sides came to an agreement, but Clark deserves the credit for that. The deal also raised questions about whether the new CBA was financially responsible. Time will tell. 6. Napheesa Collier's attack on Engelbert Then came the moment that arguably did the most damage to Engelbert's reputation among players. In September 2025, Minnesota Lynx star and WNBPA vice president Napheesa Collier publicly delivered a devastating criticism of league leadership. Collier accused the WNBA of poor leadership, inadequate accountability and failing to properly address player concerns. Her most memorable assessment was that the WNBA had "the worst leadership in the world." She specifically criticized Engelbert over officiating, player safety, compensation and communication. Collier also described conversations with Engelbert in which she said her concerns weren't taken seriously. Engelbert disputed some of Collier's characterization of their conversations but ultimately acknowledged that she needed to do better and rebuild trust with the players. Notably, Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham criticized Engelbert in August, calling her a "delusional leader" and stating the league needs a "bold" commissioner who prioritizes players over self-interest. You'd be hard pressed to find another commissioner with a worse relationship with players. 7. The transgender-athlete controversy Engelbert also became involved in one of the most politically sensitive issues in American sports: male participation in women's athletics. The WNBA faced growing questions about eligibility rules, biological sex and the participation of transgender athletes. Engelbert put together a task force that has amounted to absolutely nothing, other than providing a clear indication that she and WNBA leadership are so captured by left-wing politics and ideology that neither Engelbert nor the task force can publicly admit that the W in WNBA stands for women and that the proper definition of the word is adult human females. Fans have been discriminated against for wearing XX-XY T-shirts; Enes Kanter Freedom was confronted by Natasha Cloud for wearing a shirt defining what a woman is; and teenagers sitting courtside in XX-XY T-shirts were verbally abused by a co-owner of the Seattle Storm. Cunningham has been on the receiving end of hard fouls, relentless booing and more since she said men don’t belong in women’s sports and spaces. In this moment, the WNBA needs a leader to cool the temperature, but Engelbert has failed time and time again. Engelbert's legacy The league has historically positioned itself as more than a sports organization, taking strong positions on racial justice, reproductive rights, LGBTQ issues and other divisive, left-wing social causes. That alienates fans and is not a good business model. Engelbert will be remembered for allowing the league to be known as the most politically active and divisive in American pro sports. The WNBA claims to be a league that welcomes everyone, yet some fans and even players increasingly feel that certain political viewpoints aren’t welcome. That’s a problem for which Engelbert is to blame. In 2026, debates over fan behavior, political speech, men in women's sports and other controversies have become almost as prominent as the basketball itself. You can thank Engelbert for that. The WNBA needs a competent leader who understands business, wants to unite fans around basketball and, most importantly, embraces and markets Caitlin Clark. I won’t hold out much hope for that, though.

articles.title: LSU holds off on adding players with NFL ties as SEC lawsuit looms over program, Lane Kiffin
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers held off adding former Ole Miss players to the roster Friday as the SEC's federal lawsuit and punishment threats intensified.
articles.body: BATON ROUGE, La. - The ongoing battle between LSU and the SEC reached a tipping point Thursday when the conference filed a federal lawsuit against the school over Lane Kiffin’s potential addition of players with NFL ties. On Thursday, plaintiffs were granted a preliminary injunction by Judge William Jorden of the 19th District Court of Louisiana that allows them to be rostered by different schools for the upcoming season. Because of this ruling, all eyes were on a Friday deadline in which schools are required to submit their rosters before their official season begins. INSIDE A LOUISIANA COURTROOM: SEC-LSU LEGAL CIRCUS PLAYED OUT LIKE A JOHN GRISHAM NOVEL IN STUNNING SHOWDOWN But, lost in the arguments around this deadline was an exemption the SEC enacted this past April that allows a team to add players to their roster if they are currently enrolled in classes as a full-time student. According to multiple sources, LSU did not add Dae'Quan Wright or Zxavian Harris to its roster on Friday, but have the option to add them at a later time. This could come at any point over the course of the season, but would most likely happen sooner rather than later, if they do at all. There was also a number of intense conversations had on Friday surrounding this situation, with the SEC hellbent on punishing LSU if they were to have added the players to their official roster. What began as a lawsuit filed by members of the 2022 recruiting class seeking an additional season of eligibility has now escalated into a legal battle involving five different parties. The dispute stems from the NCAA’s new "five-for-five" eligibility rule, which stipulates that athletes have five years to play five seasons of college sports. JUDGE GRANTS INJUNCTION AGAINST NCAA, SEC, ALLOWING ATHLETES WITH NFL TIES ELIGIBLE TO PLAY FOR LSU, OTHERS Some of those athletes granted protection by the court included former Ole Miss football players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who both told OutKick that they were under the impression that the Tigers would be adding them to the roster for the upcoming season. This followed a highly contentious hearing that involved SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey, who testified that any school in the conference that rostered players with professional ties would be violating newly created rules pertaining to the eligibility of those with NFL experience. In a shocking turn of events that started just three minutes after Sankey took the stand, the SEC had already filed a federal lawsuit in a North Alabama court against LSU, Lane Kiffin and other school administrators for violating the SEC's first amendment rights to enforce conference rules. "We established our First Amendment right for freedom of association, so that our conference can make decisions and our members can make decisions about membership," Sankey said under oath when asked about the SEC filing the lawsuit. INSIDE A LOUISIANA COURTROOM: SEC-LSU LEGAL CIRCUS PLAYED OUT LIKE A JOHN GRISHAM NOVEL IN STUNNING SHOWDOWN Decision on LSU rostering athletes came down to school officials, not football coach Now, with the conference making its stance clear, which came with SEC Presidents and Chancellors authorizing Sankey to enforce the rules with punishments that include a 50% suspension of the head coach, along with substantial fines to any school that violates the guidelines, it came down to the final hours on Friday. This decision was not made by Lane Kiffin. Multiple sources told OutKick that school administrators, along with Governor Jeff Landry and President Wade Rousse were discussing the situation with LSU legal counsel throughout Thursday evening and all of Friday. As the clock ticked on Friday, officials were still unsure as to what the Tigers football program would do as conversations between all parties involved continued. Now, with court cases continuing to play out across the country, it will be interesting to see what other schools who were thinking of taking this route are going to do. If LSU had added Wright and Harris to their roster and then taken them off down the road, attorney Ryan Downton told OutKick that he would have then returned to the same courthouse that was the epicenter of college football on Thursday to file a 'contempt of court' order against the Tigers. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP But now, with LSU deciding to not add them to the official list for the Clemson game, everyone can take a deep breath and regroup. Conversations around this matter will continue, while the SEC still has its lawsuit against LSU sitting in a federal court. Now, we can focus on the upcoming slate of college football this weekend, while lawyers for all parties involved figure out what to do next.

articles.title: A qué hora es el Mali - España: horario y dónde ver hoy en TV y online el partido del Mundial Femenino de Baloncesto
articles.standfirst: Los detalles del segundo encuentro del Mundial
articles.summary: Los detalles del segundo encuentro del Mundial
articles.body: La selección española de baloncesto femenino afronta este sábado su segundo compromiso en el Mundial tras haber firmado un debut memorable ante Alemania, a la que arrolló por 83-53 con una actuación coral impecable. Sin embargo, el equipo dirigido por Miguel Méndez llega al choque envuelto en un notable malestar debido al exigente calendario de la competición, ya que dispondrá de menos de 16 horas de descanso entre el término del primer duelo y el inicio del segundo. La alero María Conde y el propio seleccionador han expresado su disconformidad por una programación que ha obligado al cuerpo técnico a preparar las dos primeras citas de forma simultánea. Enfrente estará la selección de Mali, un rival caracterizado por su poderío físico y la presencia de jugadoras bien conocidas en la Liga Femenina Endesa como Aminata Sangaré y Sika Koné. Pese a que el antecedente más reciente en la preparación veraniega se resolvió con un holgado triunfo español, el combinado nacional deberá sobreponerse al cansancio y a la falta de la habitual sesión de tiro matinal para mantener el ritmo competitivo, imponer su fluidez en el juego exterior y asegurar una victoria que encamine su pase a la siguiente fase del torneo. El partido entre Mali y España, correspondiente a la segunda jornada de la fase de grupos del Mundial Femenino de Baloncesto, se disputará este sábado 5 de septiembre a las 11:30 horas (horario peninsular español) en el Max Schmeling Hall de Berlín. El encuentro entre Mali y España se podrá seguir en directo por televisión en abierto a través del canal Teledeporte y de forma online en la plataforma gratuita RTVE Play. Sigue toda la actualidad del Mundial Femenino de Baloncesto, el minuto a minuto del partido de España y las mejores crónicas en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Mali - España en directo | Última hora del Mundial de Baloncesto Femenino hoy, en vivo
articles.summary: Sacó los dos tiros libres Haidara para mantener los diez de ventaja. Final de un tercer cuarto que ha ganado Mali 31-19. Canastón de Mariona con pacie
articles.body:
Última hora del Mali - España en directo:

¡¡¡Muy buenos días y bienvenidos a todos y todas al Mundial Femenino de Baloncesto 2026 de Alemania !!! Apenas 18 horas después del apabullante debut, la selección española juega su segundo partido de la fase de grupos con el objetivo de encarrilar el primer puesto en el grupo A . Tras la victoria imperial de ayer ante la anfitriona (83-53) , las de Miguel Méndez disputan esta segunda prueba contra Mali , rival que ya conocen. España venció a las africanas hace justo siete días en el penúltimo partido de preparación en Zaragoza (97-58) . Mali llega con la necesidad de ganar después de caer ayer en su primer partido ante Japón (102-97), con una exhibición de récord de las niponas desde el triple, con 20 .

Respecto a España , intentará seguir con las buenas sensaciones que transmitió ayer. Un actuación coral , con mucha intensidad , gran defensa y un reseñable 50% de acierto en el triple (14/28) . A destacar el partido de Awa Fam , con 17 puntos , Iyana Martín , con 12 , Raquel Carrera , con un 10-10 y María Conde con 13 tantos , todas ellas muy acertadas desde el 6,75 .

El objetivo de España , más allá de buscar el triunfo, estará también en seguir metiendo en dinámica a aquellas jugadoras que se han unido más tarde a la concentración y que llevan pocos entrenamientos con el equipo, como es el caso de Alicia Flórez o Megan Gustafson , aparte de la propia Carrera. No obstante, a ninguna de las tres pareció pesarle en absoluto dicha cuestión.

Además, en un torneo tan corto y con tan poco descanso, Méndez también tendrá que estar pendiente de las rotaciones del equipo. En el encuentro de ayer se repartieron bastante los minutos, con Pueyo , Buenavida y Torrens como las jugadoras con menos participación, con 12 , 9 y 5 minutos respectivamente. España no tendrá ni 12 horas de descanso entre un partido y otro, y María Conde se pronunció sobre ello: "Hay que darle una vuelta al calendario. FIBA tendrá que repensarlo porque se habla de darle prioridad a los deportistas, pero no está pasando y no vamos a tener ni 12 horas para descansar ".

Con todo ello, España tendrá en el Max Schmeling Hall de Berlín su segunda puesta a punto para volver a seguir con buen pie en este torneo en el que hay tantas expectativas puestas. El balón volará al cielo de la capital alemana desde las 11.30h , y lo viviremos una vez más con todos vosotros, aquí, en MARCA .

articles.title: La selección femenina toma la plaza de Callao
articles.standfirst: De la mano de CaixaBank, la pantalla de FNAC muestra contenidos de respaldo al equipo, los marcadores en tiempo real y una experiencia interactiva abierta al público
articles.summary: De la mano de CaixaBank, la pantalla de FNAC muestra contenidos de respaldo al equipo, los marcadores en tiempo real y una experiencia interactiva abierta al público
articles.body: Durante la primera semana de septiembre, uno de los espacios más emblemáticos de la capital se viste de baloncesto. La plaza de Callao acoge durante estos días una experiencia interactiva con la que CaixaBank quiere acercar a la Selección Española Femenina de Baloncesto a madrileños y visitantes, invitándoles a vivir el paso de las jugadoras de la Selección Femenina por el Mundial de una forma participativa y a mostrar su apoyo al equipo español. Del 1 al 7 de septiembre, la pantalla gigante de FNAC Callao difunde contenidos dedicados a apoyar a las jugadoras de la Selección Española durante su paso por el Mundial de Baloncesto Femenino. En los días de partido, muestra una cuenta atrás antes del inicio de cada encuentro y el marcador en tiempo real, convirtiéndose en un punto de seguimiento del campeonato para quienes pasen por el centro de la ciudad. Además, desde ayer y hasta el 6 de septiembre, de 20:00 a 23:00 horas, la plaza ofrece una experiencia interactiva en la que cualquier persona podrá participar desde su teléfono móvil. Los usuarios tienen la oportunidad de lanzar un balón virtual a canasta y ver el resultado proyectado en la pantalla gigante de Callao, compartiendo la emoción del torneo en pleno espacio urbano. La acción se enmarca en la campaña Volvemos a Creer, con la que CaixaBank acompaña a la Selección Española Femenina en un momento especialmente ilusionante para el baloncesto nacional. Un mensaje alineado con el concepto Volvemos a Soñar impulsado por la Federación Española de Baloncesto, que pone el foco en la emoción del regreso de España a una nueva gran cita internacional y en la ilusión compartida por un equipo que aspira a volver a emocionar a toda la afición. La iniciativa se corresponde con el compromiso que CaixaBank mantiene desde hace años con el baloncesto español y, especialmente, con la promoción del baloncesto femenino. Como Socio Patrocinador de la FEB y de la Selección Española, la entidad impulsa diferentes proyectos para acercar este deporte a nuevos públicos y fomentar los valores que representa dentro y fuera de la pista. CaixaBank, patrocinador de referencia del baloncesto español CaixaBank es socio patrocinador de la Federación Española de Baloncesto (FEB) y patrocinador oficial de la selección española, tanto femenina como masculina, en todas sus categorías, que van desde la absoluta hasta la sub-16, y patrocinador principal de la Federación Española de Deportes de Personas con Discapacidad Física, con el objetivo de impulsar el baloncesto en silla de ruedas. Al mismo tiempo, la entidad financiera es patrocinadora de múltiples canteras de baloncesto en España, tanto profesionales como amateurs. A través de la vinculación con los equipos, CaixaBank promueve la práctica y la promoción del baloncesto para equipos de formación y escuelas de baloncesto en todo el territorio de influencia. Mediante estos acuerdos CaixaBank fomenta la participación en competiciones oficiales de dichos equipos, así como la organización de campus, concesiones de becas a jóvenes deportistas y formación de entrenadores. La entidad financiera lleva apoyando al baloncesto nacional desde el año 2013 y su implicación y la activación de múltiples iniciativas en torno a este deporte han ayudado a visibilizar y ampliar la repercusión de los mayores éxitos cosechados internacionalmente. En su implementación de la estrategia de patrocinio local, CaixaBank ha colaborado con los principales eventos baloncestísticos que se han celebrado en la última década en España, tanto profesionales como amateurs, trasladando los valores del deporte a todos los rincones del país. Prueba de ello es la apuesta como patrocinador oficial de la Copa del Mundo de 2014 celebrada en España, la colaboración con la Copa del Mundo de Baloncesto Femenino celebrada en Tenerife el año 2018, el Eurobasket femenino que se disputó en Valencia en 2021. Igualmente, cabe destacar el histórico compromiso con el Circuito 3x3 CaixaBank, el mayor circuito de baloncesto 3x3 en la calle que se disputa desde el año 2012, una de las competiciones de referencia del deporte base que ha congregado a 64.000 jugadores de todas las edades y que ha recibido más de 475.000 visitantes tras realizar 143 paradas en más de 50 ciudades españolas a lo largo de su historia. CaixaBank también colabora con la FEB con el fin de fomentar un programa de voluntariado deportivo que trascendiera la propia competición: el programa voluntarios FEB CaixaBank. Creado con motivo de la Copa del Mundo Masculina celebrada en España 2014, hoy en día, el programa ha conseguido tejer una sólida comunidad de cerca de 25.000 voluntarios, que dan apoyo a todos los eventos oficiales de baloncesto organizados por la FEB.

articles.title: Wanted: A new WNBA commissioner. She must be everything to everyone
articles.summary: For about 44 awkward seconds inside a nightclub, Cathy Engelbert was indeed the beloved commissioner of the WNBA. The setting: the 2025 All-Star weekend in d...
articles.body:
For about 44 awkward seconds inside a nightclub, Cathy Engelbert was indeed the beloved commissioner of the WNBA.

The setting: the 2025 All-Star weekend in downtown Indianapolis. The vibe: mixed drinks and bad decisions. The moment: Engelbert and a pair of pink-haired players, Courtney Williams and Natisha Hiedeman, streaming their 'StudBudz' shenanigans nonstop.

With the camera rolling and the DJ playing the party anthem "Knuck If You Buck," Engelbert greets the players, tells them they're "amazing," and raises both hands in a way that someone who's never given a fist bump in their life would attempt a fist bump.

Alas, the next woman who becomes WNBA commissioner — and it will be a woman — she'll have to continue this delicate dance.

Now that Engelbert has announced her decision to retire at the end of this season, she leaves with a long list of business wins and strained relationships. So the next commissioner chosen to lead this league, she'd better be a special boss . One who can show business competence and still communicate like a regular person. One who can anticipate the outside disruptions while empathizing with the targeted workforce inside the storm. Above all else, she'd better understand that the WNBA hasn't reached the finish line of being financially solvent, while still seeing the players as more than just parts of the money machine.

Since she'll be a woman required to do all this heavy lifting, she'd better accept the unfairness of it all.

Because the world is the way it is, the standard for female CEOs will always be higher and more personal than that of their male counterparts. She has to be approachable in the hallways, yet have some callousness in the boardroom. Her personality has to demand respect, but she still has to be, you know, a boss with rizz. She should be prepared to be condemned as a tyrant for making the same hard decisions a man might make, as researchers found in 2016 in coverage about then-Yahoo CEO Marissa Mayer compared with Jack Dorsey, the guy who allowed Twitter to go to hell.

Now, let's get this straight: Bad bosses are bad bosses, regardless of gender. Comedian Ellen DeGeneres lost her popular talk show for creating a toxic work environment. Former Vice President Kamala Harris ran through staffers as though she was hosting a version of "Squid Game" inside the Eisenhower Executive Office Building. New Orleans Saints and Pelicans owner Gayle Benson racked up tons of civil lawsuits from her previous day job as a licensed interior designer. So to ignore the missteps made by Engelbert, or shield any woman in a leadership position from justifiable criticism, would be the opposite of equality among the sexes. It would be condescending and a distorted version of "women helping women."

Even with that acknowledgment, however, there's still the truth about the way women leaders must walk a fine line between exercising their power without being labeled as bitchy. Mary Ann Sieghart, who authored "The Authority Gap: Why Women Are Still Taken Less Seriously Than Men, and What We Can Do About it," said during a panel last year that "women are 10 times more likely to be described as abrasive than men, while men are three to four times more likely to be described as confident than women."

Engelbert's problem wasn't that she was so abrasive. She just lacked emotional equity with the players. She tossed up word salads as messaging, and apparently, didn't seem to care. Also, it must be noted: The majority of Engelbert's critics were women.

At the end of last season, Minnesota Lynx star Napheesa Collier scorched the league by saying that the WNBA had the "worst leadership in the world." Collier also alleged that Engelbert had told her Caitlin Clark and other young stars "should be on their knees," thankful for the platform provided by the WNBA. A good boss would've viewed it the other way around, that the league should've been on its knees groveling in gratitude for the crossover stars and their impact on the overall bottom line.

The woman who'll replace Engelbert should learn from her mistakes.

Then again, who really wants to be WNBA commissioner ? It feels like an impossible job. For instance: Is the position more fit for a figurehead or an independent CEO? The crowning achievement of Engelbert's seven-plus years has to be the media rights deal the league secured under her stewardship. The deal is now worth more than $3 billion, and yet it's been reported that her boss, NBA commissioner Adam Silver, negotiated that payday — not her.

The job appears even less desirable since the WNBA attracts the crazies and the chaos more than any other professional sports league. Maybe there's a tracker inside the league office that reads: "Zero Days Since The Last Political Firestorm." If so, then just wait, because certainly some Republican lawmaker is ready to pen the next letter to the commissioner complaining about the "racially motivated" attacks against Clark.

It's now just a typical Friday night in the W when former NBA player Royce White shows up to an Indiana Fever game — wearing a long blonde wig — as part of his trolling to get drafted into the league as a "Black Trans Lesbian." As silly as White and Enes Kanter Freedom look during their cosplay as protectors of women's sports , the league still had to acknowledge their foolishness and respond that neither man is eligible for the WNBA draft. At least, the W can ban those bozos, but there's no eradicating the anonymous hate mongers across social media who direct racial and homophobic abuse at players.

Whew. Bless the brave woman who wants to inherit this burden.

For one unforgettable night in Indy, however, Engelbert had to have loved being commissioner.

As she grooved, the players swooned and cheered her on. "Look at Cathy!" Williams screamed, and Engelbert danced harder. She started to twirl. The crowd stopped and stared. More phones popped out to document this monumental scene when the chorus dropped and Engelbert instantaneously turned into an auntie.

In those moments, Engelbert wasn't the players' biggest enemy in a labor fight, nor the public's easiest target for heckles and derision. Instead, in that short clip, she was relaxed, fun, just one of the girls. For maybe the only time in her tumultuous years as the league's commissioner, Cathy Engelbert was relatable.

Quite the sobering commentary on society, but the next WNBA commissioner must understand the high-wire act of being in charge while combating the perception of not being warm enough. It's unfair, but it's the dance women leaders have danced since the beginning of time.

articles.summary: We went to NBA 2K27 to see how the OKC Thunder's 2026-27 season will play out. Here are the results.
articles.body:
After falling short in the Western Conference finals last season, the OKC Thunder is looking to reclaim its spot atop the NBA.

To see how the 2026-27 season could play out, we simulated the entire campaign 10 times on NBA 2K27 . The popular video game released globally on Friday.

Here are the results, from OKC's record to player stats to award winners to playoff runs:

OKC Thunder projected 2026-27 NBA season results

OKC's average regular-season record was 60-22. Its average finish in the Western Conference standings was second, only trailing San Antonio .

Here's a complete look at the average conference standings order:

The biggest breakout team in the West was Portland , which was led by its newly-formed backcourt duo of Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The Trail Blazers consistently won 50 games but struggled to translate that into postseason success, never reaching the conference finals.

The most disappointing team was Denver , which took a step backwards after losing Peyton Watson this summer. The Nuggets finished in the Play-In range five times, and they only reached the conference finals once.

The biggest breakout team in the East was Orlando , which found its stride under first-year head coach Sean Sweeney. The Magic had four 60-win seasons and even won one NBA championship.

The most disappointing team in the East was Philadelphia , which added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James this summer but often struggled with injuries. The 76ers missed the cut for the Play-In tournament three times and only reached the conference finals once.

articles.title: Phillies Castoff Sends Trade Ultimatum After 13-Year Career, ‘I Was Over It’
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies received an exit demand from their polarizing outfield veteran shortly before a late-season trade.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies made a series of moves to strengthen their roster for the second-half push, but not every veteran addition was destined to remain with the club through September. And one of the more notable late season acquisitions has now moved on in an unusual departure.

Veteran outfielder Tommy Pham, known as an outspoken presence in virtually every clubhouse, joined the Phillies earlier in the season and spent time at Triple-A Lehigh Valley, where he remained fairly productive while waiting for another opportunity in the majors. With the Phillies outfield situation set without him, however, that opportunity never materialized.

The Phillies ultimately traded Pham to the Chicago White Sox for cash considerations shortly before rosters expanded this month.

"The Chicago White Sox are acquiring outfielder Tommy Pham from the Philadelphia Phillies," ESPN's Jeff Passan reported at the time . "Pham is expected to join the White Sox when rosters expand Sept. 1. The 38-year-old rejoins the Sox after spending parts of 2026 with the (New York) Mets, (Baltimore Orioles) and Phils."

Now, after returning to Chicago, Pham has revealed that he was clear with the Phillies about his desire to be moved.

Former Philadelphia Phillies Outfielder Tommy Pham Reveals That He Demanded Trade

In his first interview after the trade, Pham revealed that he essentially refused to remain in the minor leagues with the Phillies.

"I wanted to give the Phillies a heads up that that was my last week in Triple-A," Pham told the Chicago Sun-Times' James Fegan. "I checked out. Being in the situation I'm in, a guy with 10-plus (years of service time) playing Triple-A like that, I was over it."

Despite his frustration, Pham had performed reasonably well for Lehigh Valley and he might have been a veteran presence that the Phillies wanted to keep were it not for his ultimatum.

"He has stepped to the plate 189 times for Lehigh Valley with just three home runs but a huge 16.9% walk rate," Darragh McDonald reported for MLB Trade Rumors . "His 20.1% strikeout rate is also a strong figure. He put up a .250/.381/.391 line with the IronPigs, with that production translating to a 110 wRC+, indicating he was 10% better than league average."

That production made his lack of a major league opportunity somewhat notable, particularly given what had appeared like an opening in the Phillies outfield when they first acquired Pham.

Philadelphia Phillies Grant Veteran Outfielder His Exit After Trade Demand

The Phillies had been searching for outfield solutions after Adolis Garcia suffered season-ending shoulder surgery, but the club ultimately addressed its roster differently. Philadelphia acquired Luis Arraez from the San Francisco Giants and moved him to the infield, while Bryce Harper shifted into right field and Brandon Marsh handled left.

That left limited room for Pham, especially with Bryan De La Cruz and Derek Hill also available as bench options and Justin Crawford emerging as a viable option.

So, while Pham's latest Triple-A performance showed he could contribute offensively, he didn't do enough to seize an everyday outfield role with the Phillies. Now, after a 13-year major league career, Pham gets another chance in Chicago after giving the Phillies little choice but to move him.

articles.title: Llegan los fichajes al Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Los blancos se miden este sábado al Kosner Baskonia en un amistoso en el que podrían estrenarse Luwawu-Cabarrot, Jantunen, Pradilla, Shulga y Jones
articles.summary: Los blancos se miden este sábado al Kosner Baskonia en un amistoso en el que podrían estrenarse Luwawu-Cabarrot, Jantunen, Pradilla, Shulga y Jones
articles.body: El Real Madrid disputa este sábado (20.00 horas) su segundo partido en la pretemporada. Los blancos se miden al Kosner Baskonia en el Palacio de Deportes de León en la primera edición del Memorial Urbano González Escapa. Será la primera oportunidad de ver a alguna de las nuevas incorporaciones del conjunto madridista. En el primer amistoso (derrota ante el Río Breogán por 110-102), el que supuso el estreno de Pedro Martínez como entrenador del Madrid, no pudieron participar los internacionales que se encontraban con sus selecciones disputando las Ventanas FIBA. Esta vez los blancos sí que podrán contar con muchos de sus fichajes. El entrenador madridista podría alinear este sábado a Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot, Mikael Jantunen, Jaime Pradilla y Max Shulga. También a Damian Jones, la última incorporación anunciada, que no estaba con su selección, sino disputando la final de la Liga de Puerto Rico con los Vaqueros de Bayamón. A esa primera cita también faltaron Andrés Feliz, Facundo Campazzo y Gabriel Deck. Este último será baja ante el conjunto baskonista después de haberse lastimado un hombro durante la Ventana FIBA con Argentina. Se le salió en el primero de los partidos y pese a todo disputó el segundo. El Madrid no ha emitido parte médico al respecto, lo que invita a pensar que no se trata de nada grave. El Baskonia llega al partido con numerosas lesiones y la plantilla pendiente de completar con más fichajes. Esa falta de efectivos puso en peligro la cita, pero finalmente se podrá disputar. Khalifa Diop acaba de poner rumbo a los Cavaliers, Markus Howard, Tadas Sedekerskis y los recién llegados AJ Lawson y DJ Stewart están tocados y Kenneth Faried aún no se ha incorporado. El entrenador Paolo Galbiati quizás sólo pueda alinear a Damion Baugh y Chris Duarte de entre sus nuevos cromos.
